the two are attached to يغرقكم. ﴿كَفَرْتُمْ﴾: the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿لا تَجِدُوا﴾: lā is negative, and an imperfect verb conjoined to what precedes it, accusative like it, by the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تبيعا. ﴿تَبِيعاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is a preposition and particle of oath [Translator's note: so in the source, although it then treats the oath as omitted], the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿كَرَّمْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿بَنِي﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative by the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. ﴿آدَمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the fatḥa because it is a diptote. ﴿وَحَمَلْناهُمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿فِي الْبَرِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حملناهم. ﴿وَالْبَحْرِ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to البر. ﴿وَرَزَقْناهُمْ﴾: conjoined to حملناهم, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رزقناهم. ﴿وَفَضَّلْناهُمْ﴾: conjoined to what preceded. ﴿عَلى كَثِيرٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فضلناهم. ﴿مِمَّنْ﴾: من is a preposition and مَن is a relative noun; the two are attached to كثير. ﴿خَلَقْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿تَفْضِيلًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq.

daas-irab:71-72.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being "واذكر" (and remember). ﴿نَدْعُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw because of heaviness, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كُلَّ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أُناسٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِإِمامِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ندعو. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أُوتِيَ﴾: a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is omitted; it is in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis). ﴿كِتابَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِيَمِينِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوتي, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and أولاء is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is for address; the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من. ﴿يَقْرَؤُنَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿كِتابَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is negative. ﴿يُظْلَمُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَتِيلًا﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "ظلما فتيلا". ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿فِي هذِهِ﴾: the hā is for drawing attention, and ذه is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive; the two are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿أَعْمى﴾: the noun of kāna, nominative by an implied ḍamma on the alif because of impossibility [Translator's note: so in the source; أعمى is usually parsed as the khabar of kāna, its noun being a latent pronoun]. ﴿فَهُوَ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and هو is mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar. ﴿أَعْمى﴾: khabar. ﴿وَأَضَلُّ﴾: conjoined to what preceded, and it is nominative like it. ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾: tamyīz (specification). The clause of the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is in the position of the jussive because it is joined to the fāʾ, and the two clauses of the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.

daas-irab:73-75.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and in is lightened (mukhaffafa) from the heavy inna, its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿كادُوا﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, one of the verbs of proximity, and the wāw is its noun. ﴿لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ﴾: the lām is the one that distinguishes between negation and affirmation (al-fāriqa), and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كادوا. ﴿عَنِ الَّذِي﴾: الذي is a relative noun, and the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb before them. ﴿أَوْحَيْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحينا. ﴿لِتَفْتَرِيَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of cause, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the lām and what follows it are attached to تفتري [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably يفتنونك is meant]. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تفتري. ﴿غَيْرَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَإِذاً﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and إذن is a particle of answer. ﴿لَاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿خَلِيلًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَلَوْلا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and لولا is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle for the future. ﴿ثَبَّتْناكَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; an and what follows it are in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "ولولا تثبيتك" (were it not for Our making you firm). ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an oath, and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿كِدْتَ﴾: an incomplete past verb, one of the verbs of proximity, and the tāʾ is its noun; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿تَرْكَنُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, and the clause is the khabar of كدت. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تركن. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿إِذاً﴾: a particle of answer. ﴿لَأَذَقْناكَ﴾: the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam) [Translator's note: so in the source; in the same sentence it treats the clause as the answer to the oath, i.e. the lām of the answer], and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿ضِعْفَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْحَياةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَضِعْفَ الْمَماتِ﴾: conjoined to what preceded. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿لا تَجِدُ﴾: lā is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجد. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نصيرا. ﴿نَصِيراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:76-78.t: ﴿وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ﴾: its i'rab has passed shortly before. ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to يستفزونك. ﴿لِيُخْرِجُوكَ﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of cause, through the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the lām and what follows it are attached to يستفزونك. ﴿مِنْها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخرجوك. ﴿وَإِذاً﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is a particle of answer. ﴿لا﴾: negative. ﴿يَلْبَثُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined, and يلبثون is the apodosis of an implied law. ﴿خِلافَكَ﴾: an adverb attached to يلبثون, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its implied form being "إلّا لبثا قليلا". ﴿سُنَّةَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, its implied form being "سنّ الله ذلك سنة". ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿قَبْلَكَ﴾: قبل is an adverb of time attached to أرسلنا, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ رُسُلِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا تَجِدُ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, lā is negative, and تجد is an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِسُنَّتِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجد, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تَحْوِيلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَقِمِ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الصَّلاةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِدُلُوكِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أقم, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source; there is no pronoun kāf in لدلوك]. ﴿الشَّمْسِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلى غَسَقِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أقم. ﴿اللَّيْلِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقُرْآنَ﴾: conjoined to الصلاة. ﴿الْفَجْرِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿الْفَجْرِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كانَ مَشْهُوداً﴾: kāna and its khabar (predicate), and its noun is omitted; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the inna clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:79-81.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to تهجد. ﴿فَتَهَجَّدْ﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to أقم. ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تهجد. ﴿نافِلَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نافلة. ﴿عَسى﴾: a complete (tāmm) past verb. ﴿أَنْ يَبْعَثَكَ﴾: an puts the verb in the accusative, and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), whose fāʿil is latent, and the kāf is its object; the clause is the fāʿil of عسى. ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: the fāʿil of يبعث, nominative (marfūʿ), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مَقاماً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because whoever "raises you" [يبعثك] "makes you stand" [يقيم]. ﴿مَحْمُوداً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of مقاما. ﴿وَقُلْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿رَبِّ﴾: the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle, accusative by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which was deleted for lightness; it is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَدْخِلْنِي﴾: a verb of supplication; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the speech reported. ﴿مُدْخَلَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿صِدْقٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ﴾: its i'rab is like the preceding one, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿وَاجْعَلْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اجعل. ﴿مِنْ لَدُنْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اجعل, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿سُلْطاناً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿نَصِيراً﴾: an adjective of سلطانا. ﴿وَقُلْ﴾: its i'rab is at the beginning of the previous verse. ﴿جاءَ الْحَقُّ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the speech reported. ﴿وَزَهَقَ الْباطِلُ﴾: conjoined to what preceded. ﴿إِنَّ الْباطِلَ﴾: inna and its noun, and the clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position. ﴿كانَ زَهُوقاً﴾: kāna and its khabar (predicate), and its noun is omitted, the implied form being "كان هو"; the clause is the khabar of inna.

daas-irab:82-84.t: ﴿وَنُنَزِّلُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to ننزل. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿هُوَ شِفاءٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to شفاء. ﴿لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رحمة. ﴿وَلا يَزِيدُ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, lā is negative, and يزيد is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿خَساراً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and إذا is an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿أَنْعَمْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلَى الْإِنْسانِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنعمنا. ﴿أَعْرَضَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَنَأى﴾: conjoined to أعرض. ﴿بِجانِبِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نأى. ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿مَسَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its object. ﴿الشَّرُّ﴾: fāʿil, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كانَ يَؤُساً﴾: kāna and its khabar, and its noun is omitted; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿يَعْمَلُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar. ﴿عَلى شاكِلَتِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يعمل, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِمَنْ﴾: من is a relative noun, and the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿هُوَ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَهْدى﴾: khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif because of impossibility; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾: tamyīz (specification).

daas-irab:85-87.t: ﴿وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَنِ الرُّوحِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to يسألونك. ﴿قُلِ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿الرُّوحِ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar (predicate). ﴿رَبِّي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and mā is negative. ﴿أُوتِيتُمْ﴾: a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنَ الْعِلْمِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوتيتم. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and in is conditional. ﴿شِئْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَنَذْهَبَنَّ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and its fāʿil is latent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿بِالَّذِي﴾: الذي is a relative noun, and the two are attached to نذهبن. ﴿أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أوحينا. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿لا تَجِدُ﴾: lā is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجد, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجد. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وكيلا. ﴿وَكِيلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction. ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رحمة, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّ فَضْلَهُ﴾: inna and its noun, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is omitted. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كبيرا. ﴿كَبِيراً﴾: the khabar of kāna; the kāna clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna, and the clause of inna and what follows it gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:88-90.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَئِنِ﴾: the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and in is conditional. ﴿اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ﴾: a past verb, the tāʾ is for the feminine, and الإنس is the fāʿil; it is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَالْجِنُّ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الإنس. ﴿عَلى﴾: a preposition. ﴿أَنْ﴾: puts the verb in the accusative. ﴿يَأْتُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the deletion of the nūn; together with an it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive (majrūr) by على, and the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِمِثْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتوا. ﴿هذَا﴾: the hā is for drawing attention, and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْقُرْآنِ﴾: badal (substitute) of the demonstrative. ﴿لا يَأْتُونَ﴾: lā is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِمِثْلِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتون. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾: the wāw is of the ḥāl, and law is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ﴾: the noun of kāna, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِبَعْضٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظهيرا. ﴿ظَهِيراً﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, the lām prepares for the oath, and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to صرفنا. ﴿فِي هذَا﴾: ذا is a demonstrative; the two are attached to صرفنا. ﴿الْقُرْآنِ﴾: badal of the demonstrative. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of an implied mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مَثَلٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَبى أَكْثَرُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿كُفُوراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَنْ﴾: puts the verb in the accusative. ﴿نُؤْمِنَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نؤمن. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿تَفْجُرَ لَنا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعاً﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative, and its fāʿil is latent; لنا and من الأرض are both attached to the verb, and ينبوعا is mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:91-93.t: ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿تَكُونَ﴾: an imperfect incomplete (nāqiṣ) verb. ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿جَنَّةٌ﴾: its postponed noun, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ نَخِيلٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of جنة. ﴿وَعِنَبٍ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نخيل. ﴿فَتُفَجِّرَ﴾: an imperfect verb conjoined to تكون, accusative (manṣūb) like it, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْأَنْهارَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿خِلالَها﴾: an adverb of place, and the hā is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿تَفْجِيراً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿تُسْقِطَ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿السَّماءَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَما﴾: the kāf is a preposition, and mā is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar). ﴿زَعَمْتَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; mā and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تسقط. ﴿كِسَفاً﴾: ḥāl. ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِيَ﴾: أو is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ; the two are attached to تأتي. ﴿وَالْمَلائِكَةِ﴾: conjoined. ﴿قَبِيلًا﴾: ḥāl. ﴿أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ﴾: أو is a conjunction, and the i'rab of this clause is like the i'rab of أو تكون لك جنة. ﴿مِنْ زُخْرُفٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of بيت. ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿تَرْقى﴾: an imperfect verb conjoined to what preceded, accusative by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility, and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي السَّماءِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ترقى. ﴿وَلَنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and lan puts the verb in the accusative. ﴿نُؤْمِنَ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِرُقِيِّكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نؤمن, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿تُنَزِّلَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied an after حتى, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تنزل. ﴿كِتاباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿نَقْرَؤُهُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is an adjective of كتابا. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle. ﴿كُنْتُ﴾: kāna and its noun. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بَشَراً﴾: the khabar of كنت. ﴿رَسُولًا﴾: an adjective.

daas-irab:94-96.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and mā is negative. ﴿مَنَعَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿النَّاسَ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾: an puts the verb in the accusative, and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an through the deletion of the nūn; an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the second mafʿūl bihi of منع. ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb of time attached (mutaʿalliq) to منع. ﴿جاءَهُمُ الْهُدى﴾: a past verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif because of impossibility; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنْ﴾: maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar). ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; an and what follows it are in the position of the nominative as the postponed fāʿil of منع, the implied form being "إلا قولهم" (except their saying). ﴿أَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and a past verb, and the Divine Name is its fāʿil; the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بَشَراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَسُولًا﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَوْ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَلائِكَةٌ﴾: the noun of kāna. ﴿يَمْشُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is an adjective of الملائكة. ﴿مُطْمَئِنِّينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَنَزَّلْنا﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of law, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ and ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾: the two prepositions and their genitive nouns are attached to نزلنا. ﴿مَلَكاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَسُولًا﴾: an adjective. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفى﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and the Divine Name is the fāʿil. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿بَيْنِي﴾: an adverb of place, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: conjoined to بيني; the clause is the speech reported. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete past verb, and its noun is omitted. ﴿بِعِبادِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خبيرا. ﴿خَبِيراً﴾: the khabar of kāna, and the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿بَصِيراً﴾: a second khabar.

daas-irab:97-98.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and من is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَهْدِ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), its sign of the jussive being the deletion of the weak letter, and the Divine Name is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of من. ﴿وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and من is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُضْلِلْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the fiʿl al-sharṭ, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿فَلَنْ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and lan puts the verb in the accusative. ﴿تَجِدَ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ, and the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of من. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to تجد. ﴿أَوْلِياءَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أولياء, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَنَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached to نحشرهم. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عُمْياً﴾: mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: so in the source; عميا is usually parsed as a ḥāl]. ﴿وَبُكْماً وَصُمًّا﴾: conjoined to what preceded. ﴿مَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿كُلَّما﴾: an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿خَبَتْ﴾: a past verb, the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿زِدْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿سَعِيراً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿جَزاؤُهُمْ﴾: khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾: anna and its noun; it and what follows it are in the position of the genitive, and the two are attached to جزاؤهم. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar. ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كفروا, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَإِذا﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and إذا is an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿كُنَّا﴾: kāna and its noun, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عِظاماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: so in the source; it is the khabar of كنا]. ﴿وَرُفاتاً﴾: conjoined to عظاما. ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and inna and its noun. ﴿لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw. ﴿خَلْقاً﴾: ḥāl. ﴿جَدِيداً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa); the speech after قالوا is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:99-100.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is interrogative, the wāw is resumptive, and lam is a particle of negation, jussive and conversion (to the past). ﴿يَرَوْا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي﴾: anna, and the Divine Name is its noun, and the relative noun is an adjective (ṣifa); anna and what follows it take the place of the two objects of يروا. ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السموات. ﴿قادِرٌ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of anna. ﴿عَلى أَنْ يَخْلُقَ﴾: an puts the verb in the accusative, and an imperfect verb, accusative, and its fāʿil is latent; an and what follows it are in the position of the genitive, and the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to قادر. ﴿مِثْلَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَجَعَلَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جعل. ﴿أَجَلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿لا رَيْبَ﴾: lā is the lā of generic negation, and ريب is its noun. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar, and the clause is an adjective of أجلا. ﴿فَأَبَى الظَّالِمُونَ إِلَّا كُفُوراً﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and أبى is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility, and الظالمون is the fāʿil, and إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and كفورا is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَوْ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾: tawkīd (emphasis) of the fāʿil omitted together with its verb, because law enters upon the verb, and the clause [Translator's note: so in the source]; the omitted clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَمْلِكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya). ﴿خَزائِنَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَحْمَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِذاً﴾: a particle of answer. ﴿لَأَمْسَكْتُمْ﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of law, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of law. ﴿خَشْيَةَ﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿الْإِنْفاقِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَكانَ الْإِنْسانُ قَتُوراً﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar, and the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:101-102.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿مُوسى﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility. ﴿تِسْعَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آياتٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿فَسْئَلْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined. ﴿بَنِي﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative by the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa because it is a diptote. ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَقالَ لَهُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to it. ﴿فِرْعَوْنُ﴾: fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنِّي﴾: inna and its noun, and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لَأَظُنُّكَ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the kāf is its first object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿يا مُوسى﴾: يا is a vocative particle, and موسى is a vocative, a single proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied ḍamma on the alif because of impossibility, in the position of the accusative as a vocative; the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿مَسْحُوراً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of أظن. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of realisation. ﴿عَلِمْتَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما أَنْزَلَ﴾: mā is negative, and a past verb. ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾: the hā is for drawing attention, and أولاء is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿رَبُّ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السموات, and the clause takes the place of the two objects of علمت. ﴿بَصائِرَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), and the oath clause is in the position of the accusative as the speech reported. ﴿وَإِنِّي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَأَظُنُّكَ﴾: the shifted lām, and أظنك is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the kāf is its first object; the clause is the khabar. ﴿يا فِرْعَوْنُ﴾: يا is a vocative particle, and فرعون is a vocative, indeclinable on the ḍamma. ﴿مَثْبُوراً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:103-106.t: ﴿فَأَرادَ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنْ﴾: puts the verb in the accusative. ﴿يَسْتَفِزَّهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أن يستفزهم and what follows it are in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to يستفزهم. ﴿فَأَغْرَقْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: من is a relative noun conjoined to the hāʾ in أغرقناه. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾: mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of place attached to the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَقُلْنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قلنا. ﴿لِبَنِي﴾: the lām is a preposition, and بني is genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; the two are attached to قلنا. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اسْكُنُوا الْأَرْضَ﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb of time. ﴿جاءَ وَعْدُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْآخِرَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿جِئْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the speech reported [Translator's note: so in the source; it is the apodosis of إذا within the reported speech]. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جئنا. ﴿لَفِيفاً﴾: ḥāl. ﴿وَبِالْحَقِّ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزلناه. ﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَبِالْحَقِّ نَزَلَ﴾: conjoined to what preceded, and its i'rab is like it; the fāʿil of نزل is latent. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is negative. ﴿أَرْسَلْناكَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مُبَشِّراً﴾: ḥāl. ﴿وَنَذِيراً﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to مبشرا. ﴿وَقُرْآناً﴾: mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَرَقْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is explicative (mufassira). ﴿لِتَقْرَأَهُ﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied an after it, and its fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the lām and what follows it are a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فرقناه. ﴿عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقرأه. ﴿عَلى مُكْثٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَنَزَّلْناهُ تَنْزِيلًا﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil, its object and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:107-109.t: ﴿قُلْ آمِنُوا﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive; and an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to آمنوا. ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾: prohibitive. ﴿تُؤْمِنُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna. ﴿أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾: a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and it is its first object, and العلم is its second object. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوتوا, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿يُتْلى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif because of impossibility, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتلى. ﴿يَخِرُّونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of إذا; إذا and its two clauses are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the inna clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِلْأَذْقانِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخرون. ﴿سُجَّداً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿رَبِّنا﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنْ﴾: lightened (mukhaffafa) from inna, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿كانَ وَعْدُ﴾: kāna and its noun, and the clause is the khabar of in. ﴿رَبِّنا﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَمَفْعُولًا﴾: the lām that distinguishes between negation and affirmation (al-fāriqa), and ﴿مفعولا﴾ is the khabar of kāna; the clause is the khabar of in. ﴿وَيَخِرُّونَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِلْأَذْقانِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخرون. ﴿يَبْكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl, i.e. "باكين" (weeping). ﴿وَيَزِيدُهُمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is its first object. ﴿خُشُوعاً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:110-111.t: ﴿قُلِ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿ادْعُوا اللَّهَ﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and the Divine Name is its object. ﴿أَوِ ادْعُوا الرَّحْمنَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿أَيًّا﴾: a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ما﴾: redundant (zāʾida). ﴿تَدْعُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis). ﴿فَلَهُ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْأَسْماءُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْحُسْنى﴾: an adjective (ṣifa), and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis). ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَجْهَرْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِصَلاتِكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجهر, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلا تُخافِتْ﴾: conjoined to ولا تجهر, and its i'rab is like its i'rab. ﴿بِها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تخافت. ﴿وَابْتَغِ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the weak letter, and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to ابتغ. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: ذا is a demonstrative, muḍāf ilayhi, the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَقُلِ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr) by the lām; the two are attached to the khabar, and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive as an adjective. ﴿لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَلَداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلَمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and lam is a particle of jussive, negation and conversion (to the past). ﴿يَكُنْ﴾: an imperfect incomplete (nāqiṣ) verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿شَرِيكٌ﴾: the noun of يكن. ﴿فِي الْمُلْكِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شريك. ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلِيٌّ﴾: its i'rab is like the preceding one, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيراً﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is its object, and تكبيرا is mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾ (glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque): the whole sanctuary (al-ḥaram) is a mosque, meaning Mecca and its sanctuary. ﴿إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلأَقْصَى﴾ (to the Farthest Mosque): Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). ﴿ٱلَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ﴾ (whose surroundings We have blessed): with fruits and rivers.
His saying: ﴿لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَآ﴾ (to show him some of Our signs) means the Prophet ﷺ, when He took him by night to show him wonders that night. He was shown the prophets, so that he described them to the people of Mecca. They said: "We have camels on the road to Syria; tell us about them." So he told them signs and marks. They said: "When will they arrive?" He said: "On such-and-such a day, at sunrise, led by a grey (awraq) camel." They said: "These are signs by which we shall know whether he is truthful or lying." So they went out early beyond the ʿAqaba pass to meet them. One said: "By Allah, here is the sun, it has risen, and it has not come." Another said: "By Allah, here is the caravan, led by a grey camel, just as Muhammad ﷺ said." Yet they still did not believe.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَدْعُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ﴾ (and man prays): the wāw has been dropped from it in pronunciation but not in meaning, since it is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ); its dropping is due to its meeting the vowelless lām. Similar are ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾ (We will call the guards of Hell), likewise ﴿وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللّهُ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (and Allah will give the believers), His saying ﴿يَوْمَ يُنَادِ المُنَادِ﴾ (the day the caller calls), and His saying ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾ (but warnings do not avail). Had they been written with yāʾ and wāw it would have been correct. This is part of the speech of the Arabs. The poet said:
كفاك كفٌّ ما تُليق درهما * جُوداً وأخرى تُعْطِ بالسيف الدَّما
(Your two palms: one that, out of generosity, does not hold on to a dirham, and another that gives blood with the sword.)
And one of the Anṣār said:
ليس تخفى بشَارتى قَدْر يومٍ * ولقد تُخْفِ شِيمتى إعْسَارِى
(My cheerfulness is not hidden for a single day, and my character does hide my poverty.)
His saying: ﴿وَيَدْعُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ بِٱلشَّرِّ دُعَآءَهُ بِٱلْخَيْرِ﴾ (and man prays for evil as he prays for good): He means: like his praying for good, in appealing to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for something whose answering the one who prays would not like, such as his praying against his child; so he is not answered in the evil even though he prayed for it. That too is one of Allah's favours, Mighty and Majestic, upon him.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَحَوْنَآ آيَةَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ (and We erased the sign of the night): Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Mindal ibn ʿAlī told me, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad al-Dīlī, tracing it back to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: it is the smudge that is on the moon.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَآئِرَهُ﴾ (and every human being — We have fastened his omen to him): that is his deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. (وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ) (and We will bring forth for him): Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it with nūn, and others read it with yāʾ with fatḥa: (وَيَخْرُجُ لَهُ) (and there will come forth for him) — his omen; among them Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan. Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read (ويُخرِج... له كِتاباً), meaning: and He brings forth for him his deeds as a book. All of them are good.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱقْرَأْ كِتَٰبَكَ﴾ (read your book): in it — and Allah knows best — (يُقَال) ("it will be said") is suppressed. It is like His saying ﴿ويَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ أدْخِلُوا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ (and on the day the Hour arrives: "Admit the people of Pharaoh…"), and like His saying ﴿فَأَمَّا الذِينَ اسْوَدَّتْ وُجوهُهُمْ أَكَفَرْتُمْ﴾ (as for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve…?"); the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: so it will be said: "Did you disbelieve?"
His saying: ﴿كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيباً﴾ (sufficient is your own self against you this day as an accountant): in everything in the Qurʾān such as His saying ﴿وكَفَى بربّك﴾ (and sufficient is your Lord), ﴿وكفى بالله﴾ (and sufficient is Allah) and ﴿كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾, if you dropped the bāʾ the word would be nominative; as the poet said:
ويخبرنى عن غائب المَرْء هَدْيُه * كفى الهَدْىُ عَمَّا غَيَّب المرءُ مُخبِرا
(A man's conduct tells me about what is hidden in him; conduct suffices as an informant about what a man conceals.)
The bāʾ may only come in on the nominative when its owner is being praised by it; do you not see that you say: كفاكَ به (it suffices you), نهاكَ به (it restrains you), أكرِم به رجلاً (how noble a man he is), بِئس به رجلا (how bad a man he is), نعم به رجلا (how excellent a man he is), طاب بطعامك طعاماً (how good your food is as food), and جَاد بثوبك ثوباً (how fine your garment is as a garment). If it were not praise or blame it could not come in; do you not see that one who says "your brother stood" (قامَ أخوكَ) or "your brother sat" (قعد أخوك) may not say قام بأخيك or قَعَد بأخيك — unless he means that someone else stood with him and sat with him.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا﴾ (We commanded its affluent ones): al-Aʿmash [99a] «[Translator's note: "99 ا" is a manuscript folio marker.]», ʿĀṣim and men from the people of Medina read ﴿أَمَرْنا﴾ with the light form. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told me, from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj, from Mujāhid: ﴿أمَرْنا﴾ with the light form. Some explained ﴿أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا﴾ as (commanding them) to obedience, ﴿فَفَسَقُوا﴾ (but they transgressed), i.e. when the affluent person is commanded to obey, he turns instead to transgression. In the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: (بعثنا فيها أكابر مجرميها) (We raised up in it the chief of its criminals). Al-Ḥasan read ﴿آمَرنا﴾, and ﴿أَمِرْنا﴾ is also reported from him, but we do not know whether that was preserved from him correctly, because we do not know its meaning here. The meaning of (آمرنا), with the long vowel, is: We made (them) many. Abū al-ʿĀliya al-Riyāḥī read (أمَّرنا مُتْرَفيها) (We gave authority to its affluent ones), and that agrees with Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation, for he said: We set its chiefs in power, and they transgressed in it.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَآءُ لِمَن نُّرِيدُ﴾ (We hasten for him in it whatever We will, for whom We intend): i.e. that is from Us, for whom We intend.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ تَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِي وَكِيلاً﴾ (that you take no guardian besides Me): it is said: a lord; and it is said: one who suffices.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿كُلاًّ نُّمِدُّ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾ (each We provide, these [and those]): "We provide" (نُمدّ) is made to fall on both, i.e. We provide for all of them; i.e. We sustain the believer and the disbeliever from the bounty of your Lord.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا﴾ (O descendants of those We carried) is accusative on the basis of the nidāʾ (vocative). He addressed them: "O descendants of those We carried with Noah", meaning (those) in the loins of men and the wombs of women who had not yet been created.

farraa:4-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ (and We decreed for the Children of Israel): We informed them that they would cause corruption twice.
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ أُولاهُمَا﴾ (so when the promise of the first of them came): he says: the punishment for the first of the two times, which is the first of the two corruptions. ﴿بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَاداً لَّنَآ﴾ (We sent against you servants of Ours) means Nebuchadnezzar (Bukhtanaṣṣar), who took captives and killed.
His saying: ﴿فَجَاسُواْ خِلاَلَ ٱلدِّيَارِ﴾ (and they probed through the homes) means: they killed you among your houses. (فجاسُوا) has the meaning of "they seized"; and حاسوا, with ḥāʾ, is also used in that meaning.

farraa:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ ٱلْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (then We gave you back the turn against them) means against Nebuchadnezzar: a man came whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent against Nebuchadnezzar and killed him, and Allah restored to them their kingdom and their affairs. So they lived on, then they caused corruption, and that was the last of the two corruptions.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلآخِرَةِ لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ (then when the final promise came, [We sent them] to disgrace your faces): someone may ask: where is the answer (jawāb) of (إذا)? There are two aspects to it. It is said: "So when the final promise came, We sent them, so that Allah might disgrace your faces" — for whoever reads it with yāʾ. It may also be: "so that the punishment might disgrace your faces". Ubayy ibn Kaʿb [98b] «[Translator's note: "98 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]» read it (لِنَسُوءنْ وُجُوهَكُمْ) with the light form, meaning the nūn. If you made its lām take fatḥa, it would be the answer of إذا without a suppressed verb; you say: إذا أتيتنى لأسُوءَنَّكَ (when you come to me I shall certainly grieve you). The coming in of the wāw in what follows ﴿لنسوءن﴾ would then be like His saying ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُرِى إبراهيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّمَوَاتِ والأَرض ولِيَكُونَ من﴾ (and thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be among …), i.e. "We showed him the dominion (so that he might be…)"; likewise the wāw in ﴿وليَدْخُلُوا﴾ (and that they might enter): you suppress a verb for it after it. It has also been read (لِيُسوءُوا وُجُوهَكُم) — (namely) those who enter.

farraa:9-10.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ يَِهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ﴾ (indeed this Qurʾān guides to that which is most upright).
He says: to the testimony that there is no god but Allah.
﴿وَيُبَشِّرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (and gives glad tidings to the believers): the glad tidings are made to fall upon His saying ﴿أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْراً كَبِيراً﴾ (that they will have a great reward). It is also possible that the believers were given glad tidings as well by His saying ﴿وأَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً﴾ (and that those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared for them a painful punishment), because speech allows you to say: "I gave ʿAbdallāh the glad tidings that he will be given and that his enemy will be denied." And it may be: "and He gives those who do not believe in the Hereafter the tidings that We have prepared for them a painful punishment", even though He did not make the tidings fall upon them as He made them fall upon the believers before (أنَّ). It would then be like your saying in speech: "I announced that rain is coming", which contains the meaning "I announced to the people that rain is coming", even though you do not mention them. If you began afresh with ﴿وإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ (with kasra), that would be sound, but I have not heard anyone read it so.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلاَّ تَعْبُدُوۤاْ﴾ (and your Lord has decreed that you worship none [but Him]) is like your saying "your Lord has commanded". In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (وَأَوْصى رَبُّك) (and your Lord has enjoined), and Ibn ʿAbbās said it is (وَوَصَّى), its wāw having become joined (to the ṣād). The Arabs say: "I left him deciding (يقضى) people's affairs", i.e. giving orders in them, and his order is carried out.
His saying ﴿وَبِٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً﴾ (and to parents, good treatment): its meaning is: and He enjoined good treatment of parents. The Arabs say: أُوصيك به خيراً (I enjoin you to do him good) and آمرك به خيراً (I command you to do him good). Its meaning was: I command you to do (good) to him; then you drop (أنْ) and attach "good" (الخير) directly to the enjoining and to the commanding. The poet said:
عجبتُ من دَهْماء إذ تشكُونَا * ومن أبى دَهماء إذ يوصينَا * خيراً بها كأننا جافونا *
(I marvelled at Dahmāʾ when she complained about us, and at Dahmāʾ's father when he enjoined us to treat her well, as though we were treating her harshly.)
His saying: ﴿إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ﴾ (if they reach old age with you): it is put in the dual because the two parents were mentioned before it, so the verb came to match their number; «[Translator's note: the remark about the dual refers to the reading يَبْلُغانِّ, although the text here quotes the verse as يَبْلُغَنَّ.]» then He said ﴿أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْ كِلاَهُمَا﴾ (one of them or both of them) as a fresh start (iʾtināf), like His saying ﴿ثمَّ عموا وصَمُّوا﴾ (then they became blind and deaf), after which He began afresh and said ﴿كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ (many of them); and likewise His saying ﴿لاَهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وأسَرُّوا النَّجْوى﴾ (their hearts distracted, and they conferred in secret), after which He began afresh and said ﴿الذين ظَلَمُوا﴾ (those who did wrong). Many people read it ﴿إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ﴾, making ﴿يَبْلُغَنّ﴾ a verb belonging to "one of them", so you repeated «both of them» on it. «[Translator's note: the text has "فَكرَّرت ب فكرت", i.e. an editorial variant: manuscript B reads فكرت.]»
His saying ﴿فَلاَ تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ﴾ (then do not say to them "uff"): ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd and al-Aʿmash read it (أُفِّ), with the genitive vowel (khafḍ) and without nunation. The generality read (أُفٍّ). Those who gave it kasra with nunation took the view that it is a sound whose meaning is known only by uttering it, so they gave it kasra as sounds are given kasra. Among that is the Arabs' saying: "I heard ṭāqin ṭāqin" for the sound of striking, and they say: "I heard tighin tighin" for the sound of laughter. Those who did not nunate but gave it kasra said: أفّ has three letters, while most sounds have only two letters, like صَهْ, يَغْ and مَهْ; that is the kind which takes kasra and nunation, because its first letter is vowelled. We are not compelled to give a vowel to the second letter of particles (adawāt) and the like, so that it would take kasra with nūn; and أفَّ was likened to your saying مُدَّ and رُدَّ, since it consists of three letters. What indicates this is that some Arabs have given it ḍamma, saying: أفُّ لك. Similar is the saying of the rajaz poet:
سألتُها الوصلَ فقالت مِضَّ * وحَرَّكت لى رأسهَا بالنَغْض
(I asked her for union and she said "miḍḍ!", and shook her head at me in refusal.)
— like a speaker saying (لا) (no) with his molars. And it is said: "Your family taught you nothing but (مضِّ and مِضُّ)", and some of them: "nothing but مِضّا", making the verb fall on it. Some Arabs have said: "Do not say to him أُفّا or تُفّا", treating it like a noun, so it takes the genitive, the nominative [and the accusative] «[Translator's note: the text adds "ثبت فى ب", i.e. the bracketed word is found in manuscript B.]»; and the accusative without nūn is permitted, as they said رُدَّ. The Arabs say: "he began to say 'uff' (يتأفّف) at a smell he found", meaning he says: أفِّ أفِّ. The poet said, concerning what is nunated:
وقفنا فقلنا إِيهِ عن أمّ سالمٍ * وَمَا بالُ تكليم الديار البلاقع
(We halted and said: "Tell on about Umm Sālim!" — but what use is speaking to empty abodes?)
He dropped the nūn because it is like a particle; when it has three letters it is likened to their saying: جَيْرِ لا أفعل ذلك (indeed, I will not do that). The poet said:
فقُلْن عَلَى الفِردوس أوَّلُ مشرب * أَجَلْ جَيْرِ إِن كَانت أُبيحت دَعَاثرُهْ
(They said: "At al-Firdaws is the first watering-place." — Yes, indeed, if its old cisterns have been made free to use.)

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ﴾ (and lower to them the wing of humility): the generality read it with ḍamma. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym told me, from Abū Bishr Jaʿfar ibn Iyās, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he read (وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاح الذِّلّ) with kasra. He said: al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr told me, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, that he read it (الذِّلّ) with kasra. Abū Zakariyyā «[Translator's note: i.e. al-Farrāʾ himself.]» said: I asked Abū Bakr about it and he said: ʿĀṣim read it with ḍamma. الذُلّ (dhull), from الذلّة, is to humble oneself while not being lowly by nature. الذِّلَّة and الذُّلّ are the maṣdar (verbal noun) of الذليل (the lowly), and الذِّلّ (dhill) is the maṣdar of الذلول (the tractable), as with a riding animal and the ground. You say: a tractable camel (جَمَلٌ ذَلُول), a tractable riding animal, and tractable ground, clearly showing الذِّلّ.

farraa:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾ (and if you turn away from them, awaiting mercy from your Lord): he says: when your relatives or other needy people come to you asking, and you turn away because you have nothing to give them, then say to them a gentle word (قولا ميْسُوراً), he says: make them a good promise. Then He forbade him to give away all he has, so that he would not be left مَحْسوراً (exhausted), with nothing left. The Arabs say of a camel: "it is محسور" when its going has given out; and "I exhausted (حَسرت) the riding animal" when you rode it until its going gave out. And His saying: ﴿يَنْقَلِبْ إليْكَ البَصَرُ خَاسِئاً وهو حَسِيرٌ﴾ (your sight will return to you humbled and fatigued): it becomes fatigued at the farthest reach of the view.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿خِطْئاً كَبِيراً﴾ (a great sin): al-Ḥasan read خَطَاءً كبيراً, with the long vowel. Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read ﴿خَطَأْ كَبيراً﴾, short and with hamza. All are correct. It seems that الخِطْأ is sin; it may also have the meaning of خَطَأ (with the short vowel), as they said قِتْب and قَتَب (saddle), حِذُرٌ and حَذَرٌ (caution), نِجْسٌ and نَجَسٌ (impure). Similar is the reading of whoever read ﴿هُمْ أُولاَءَ عَلَى أَثَرِى﴾ (they are close upon my track) and ﴿إِثْرِى﴾.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن قُتِلَ مَظْلُوماً فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَاناً﴾ (and whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority): in retaliation or in accepting blood-money. Then He said: ﴿فَلاَ يُسْرِف فِّي ٱلْقَتْلِ﴾ (but let him not exceed limits in killing): it has been read with tāʾ and with yāʾ. Whoever read it with yāʾ referred it to the heir, i.e. he must not kill anyone other than the killer; He says: so let the heir not exceed limits in killing. He said: al-Farrāʾ «[Translator's note: the text has "القراء"; evidently al-Farrāʾ is meant.]» told us: more than one person told me — among them Mindal, Jarīr and Qays — from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān, that he read ﴿فَلاَ تُسْرِف﴾ with tāʾ. In the reading of Ubayy: (فلاَ يُسْرِفوا فىِ القتل) (so let them not exceed limits in killing).
His saying ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُوراً﴾ (indeed he has been supported): it is said: his heir has been supported. It is also said that the hāʾ (the pronoun) refers to the blood: the blood of the slain has been supported because he was wronged. The hāʾ may also refer to the slain person himself, or to the killing, since it is an act and so runs the same course as the blood. And Allah knows best which of that is right.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ﴾ (until he reaches his maturity): Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الأشُدّ is between eighteen and thirty.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْفُ﴾ (and do not pursue): most readers take it from قفوت, the fāʾ being vowelled toward the wāw, so you say ﴿وَلاَ تَقْفُ﴾. Some said (وَلاَ تَقَفْ). The Arabs say قُفْت أثره and قَفَوته (I followed his track). Similar are يَعْتام and يَعْتمى (he chooses); قاع الجملُ الناقةَ قوعاً «[Translator's note: the text has "وقعا".]» when it mounts her; and عاث and عَثَى (of causing corruption). This is frequent; among it are شاكُ السلاح and شاكى السلاح (bristling with weapons), and جُرف هارٌ and هارٍ (a crumbling bank). I heard some of Quḍāʿa say: اجتحى ماله (he swept away his wealth), while the widespread usage is اجتاح ماله. The poet said:
ولو أنى رأيتك من بعيد * لعاقكَ من دعاء النِّيب عَاقى
(Had I seen you from afar, something hindering would have kept you from calling to the old she-camels.)
He means: عائق (a hindrance).
حَسِبت بُغَام راحلتى عَنَاقاً * وما هى وَيْبَ غَيرِكَ بالعَنَاق
(You took the moan of my riding camel for a young she-goat — woe to someone other than you — it is no young she-goat.)

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿كُلُّ ذٰلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً﴾ (all that — its evil is ever hateful with your Lord): some of the people of the Ḥijāz read (كَانَ سَيِّئةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً) (was an evil, hateful with your Lord).

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ ٱلسَّبْعُ﴾ (the seven heavens glorify Him): most readers have tāʾ. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (سَبَّحتْ له السموات السبع) (the seven heavens glorified Him), and this strengthens those who read with tāʾ. Had it been read with yāʾ it would have been correct, just as they read ﴿تَكَادُ السَّمَوَاتْ﴾ (the heavens almost …) and ﴿يَكُاد﴾.
The yāʾ is good only because it is a small number; when the number of feminines or masculines is small, yāʾ is better in it than tāʾ. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said of a small feminine number: ﴿وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِى المَدِيِنَةِ﴾ (and women in the city said), and He said of the masculine: ﴿فإذا انْسَلَخَ الأشْهُرُ الحُرُمُ﴾ (and when the sacred months have passed), using the masculine. That is because the beginning of the verb of a feminine (subject), when it is few, is with yāʾ, so one says: النسوة يقمن (the women stand) [100b] «[Translator's note: "100 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]». When the verb comes first, the nūn drops from its end because the noun is overt, and the verb keeps its beginning on yāʾ. Whoever uses the feminine takes the view that (هذه) (this, feminine) applies to the plural, so he uses the feminine on account of the femininity of (هذه); and the masculine is like the feminine in this: do you not see that you say: هذه الرجال (these men) and هذه النساء (these women)? Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, from ʿAmmār al-Duhnī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: every tasbīḥ (glorification) in the Qurʾān is prayer, and every sulṭān (authority) is proof; this is on account of «[Translator's note: so the text (هذا لقوله); the connection to what precedes is unclear, and some editions may read it as an exception.]» His saying ﴿وَإِن مِّن شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ (and there is nothing but glorifies Him with praise).
His saying: ﴿عِظَاماً وَرُفَاتاً﴾ (bones and crumbled particles): الرُّفَات is dust; it has no singular, like الدُقَاق (fine fragments) and الحُطَام (debris).

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوْ خَلْقاً مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ (or some creation of what is great in your breasts): they said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Tell us, if we were death itself, who would make us die?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿أَوْ خَلْقاً مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾, meaning death itself, i.e. Allah would send against you one who would make you die. «[Translator's note: the text has "فأنز", evidently فأنزل.]»
His saying ﴿فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إِلَيْكَ رُؤُوسَهُمْ﴾ (then they will shake their heads at you): one says أَنغض رأسَه, i.e. he moved it upwards and downwards. Abū Zakariyyā showed us that: he gestured with his head, pressing it against his throat and then raising it as though looking at the ceiling. The head يَنْغَض and يَنْغِض (shakes). When a front tooth moves, it is said: نَغَضت سِنّه (his tooth became loose). The male ostrich is called نَغْض only because, when it hurries its walk, it rises and falls.
His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هُوَ﴾ (and they say: "When is it?") means the resurrection.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلاً﴾ (and We have not sent you over them as a guardian): he says: a keeper and a lord.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿زَبُوراً﴾ (the Psalms): al-Farrāʾ said: Abū Bakr told me: ʿĀṣim used to read ﴿زَبُوراً﴾ with fatḥa throughout the Qurʾān, and Ḥamza read it with ḍamma.

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿أُولَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ﴾ (those whom they invoke seek a means of access to their Lord) means the jinn whom Khuzāʿa used to worship. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿أُولَـٰئِكَ﴾, meaning the jinn whom (they invoke) seek (access) to Allah. Thus ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ is a verb belonging to those who worship them, and ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ﴾ is a verb belonging to the jinn, by which they (أولئك) are made nominative.

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوهَا﴾ (and there is no town but We shall destroy it): by death; ﴿أَوْ مُعَذِّبُوهَا عَذَاباً شَدِيداً﴾ (or punish it with a severe punishment): by the sword.

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرْسِلَ بِٱلآيَاتِ﴾ (and nothing prevented Us from sending the signs): (أنْ) is in the position of the accusative. ﴿إِلاَّ أَن كَذَّبَ﴾ (except that [the former peoples] denied them): أنْ is in the position of the nominative; just as you say: ما منعهم الإيمانَ إلاّ تكذيبُهم (nothing kept them from faith except their denial).
His saying ﴿ٱلنَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً﴾ (the she-camel as a visible sign): He made the verb (i.e. the participle) belong to her. Whoever read (مَبْصَرة) meant something like the saying of ʿAntara:
* والكفر مَخْبَثَة لنفس المنعم *
(And ingratitude is a cause of corruption to the soul of the benefactor.)
When you put mafʿala in the sense of an active participle, it does away with the plural and the feminine, so it is singular with fatḥa on its ʿayn, and kasra there is not permitted. The Arabs say: هَذا عُشْب مَلْبَنَة مَسْمنة (this is herbage that makes milk plentiful and makes fat), and: the child is مَبْخلة مَجْبنة (a cause of stinginess and cowardice). Whatever of this comes to you, produce it in this form. If it is from (a root with) yāʾ or wāw, make them overt; you say: هذا شراب مَبْوَلة (this is a drink that causes urination), هذا كلام مَهْيَبة للرجال (this is speech that makes men stand in awe), ومَتْيَهة (and a cause of going astray), and the like. The meaning of (مُبصِرة) is "giving light", as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَالنَّهَارَمُبْصِراً﴾ (and the day giving sight): giving light.

farraa:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِٱلنَّاسِ﴾ (indeed your Lord has encompassed the people) means the people of Mecca, i.e. that He will grant you victory (over them). ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا ٱلرُّؤيَا ٱلَّتِي أَرَيْنَاكَ إِلاَّ فِتْنَةً﴾ (and We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial): He means: what We showed you on the night of the Night Journey was only a trial for them, so that some of them said: "a sorcerer", "a soothsayer", and they said much (of that). ﴿وَٱلشَّجَرَةَ ٱلْمَلْعُونَةَ﴾ (and the accursed tree) is the tree of Zaqqūm; you make it accusative by جعلنا (We made). Were it made nominative, following the noun implied in "trial" from "the vision", it would be correct. Similar in ordinary speech: جَعلتك عَامِلاً وزيداً (I made you, and Zayd, an agent) and وزيدٌ.

farraa:62-62.t: His saying: ﴿لأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ (I will surely bridle his descendants, except a few): he says: I will surely gain mastery over them, ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ (except a few), meaning those who are protected (from sin).

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱسْتَفْزِزْ﴾ (and incite): he says: make light of (them) (بِصَوْتِكَ) (with your voice): with your calling. ﴿وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِم بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ﴾ (and assault them with your cavalry and your infantry) means the cavalry and the foot-soldiers of the idolaters.
His saying ﴿وَشَارِكْهُمْ فِي ٱلأَمْوَالِ وَٱلأَوْلادِ﴾ (and be a partner with them in wealth and children): every wealth mixed with what is unlawful is his share. His saying ﴿وَعِدْهُمْ﴾ (and make promises to them): i.e. tell them: there is no Paradise and no Fire. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً﴾ (and Satan promises them nothing but delusion).

farraa:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ تَجِدُواْ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا بِهِ تَبِيعاً﴾ (you would find for yourselves no avenger against Us therein): it is said: an avenger and a claimant. تَبِيع is in the sense of تابع (one who follows up).

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ نَدْعُواْ كُلَّ أُنَاسٍ بِإِمَامِهِمْ﴾ (the day We will call every people by their leader): the generality read it with nūn; and (يَدْعُو) (He will call) also, referring to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym asked me: "Is (يَوْمَ يُدْعَواْ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ) permissible?" — they had transmitted it from al-Ḥasan. I told him I did not know it. He said: "I asked the experts in Arabic about it, and they did not know it."

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن كَانَ فِي هَـٰذِهِ أَعْمَىٰ﴾ (and whoever is blind in this) means: in the blessings of this world which We have recounted to you; ﴿فَهُوَ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ (then he in the Hereafter) — in the blessings of the Hereafter — ﴿أَعْمَىٰ وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلاً﴾ (will be more blind and further astray from the way).
When the Arabs say "he is more X than you" (أفعل منك), they say it of every fāʿil and faʿīl (pattern), and of whatever verb has nothing added beyond three letters. When it is of the faʿlaltu pattern, like زخرفت (I adorned), or of the ifʿalaltu pattern, like احمررت (I became red) and اصفررت (I became yellow), they do not say "he is more X than you" (أفعل منك); they only say: "he is more intensely red than you" (أشدّ حمرةً منكَ) and "more intensely adorned than you". It was permitted with blindness here only because He did not mean blindness of the eye; He meant — and Allah knows best — blindness of the heart. So one says: "so-and-so is blinder than so-and-so in heart", and (do not say): "he is blinder than him in the eye". That is because, since it (the eye sense) comes on the pattern of أحمر/حمراء (red, masc./fem.), أفعل منك is left out of it, as it is left out of most of that kind. You may find some grammarians saying: "I permit it with الأعمى (blind), الأعشى (night-blind), الأعرج (lame) and الأزرق (blue-eyed), because we say عمِى, زرِق, عرِج and عَشِى, but we do not say صَفِر, حمِر or بَيِض." That is worth nothing. One looks in this only at that in which its owner has some action, slight or great, so that أفعل indicates the smallness or greatness of the thing; do you not see that you may say: "so-and-so is more upright (أقْوَم) than so-and-so" and "more handsome", because this one's uprightness and beauty may exceed the other's uprightness and beauty; but you do not say of two blind men: "this one is blinder than that one", nor of two dead men: "this one is deader than that one". If something of this comes to you in poetry and you allow it, both kinds can bear being allowed. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: an elder from the people of Basra told me that he heard the Arabs say: ما أسود شَعره (how black his hair is!). Al-Farrāʾ was asked about the elder and said: that is Bashshār al-Nāqiṭ. And the poet said:
أمَّا الملوكُ فأنت اليَوْمَ ألأَمُهم * لُؤماً وَأبيضُهم سِرْبالَ طبَّاخ
(As for kings, you are today the most base of them in baseness, and the whitest of them in a cook's shirt — i.e. your cook never uses it, out of stinginess.)
Whoever says this is bound to say: الله أبْيَضك (Allah made you white), والله أسْوَدك, and ما أسْوَدَك (how black you are!). There is a game of the Arabs in which they say: أَبِيضى حالا and أَسِيدى حالا. The Arabs say مُسْوِدة and مُبْيِضة (of a woman) when she gives birth to black and to white children; and mostly they say مُوضحة when she gives birth to white children, and they may say مُسِيدة. [101b] «[Translator's note: "101 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]»

farraa:76-76.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ (and indeed they were about to unsettle you from the land): when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, the Jews envied him and his presence weighed on them. So they said: "You surely know that this land is not the land of the prophets; their land is only Syria. If you are a prophet, go out to it, for Allah will grant you victory." He said: so the Prophet ﷺ encamped some miles from Medina, and Allah revealed: ﴿وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ﴾ — to make light of you — «[Translator's note: the text here repeats "وَإِذاً لاَيَلْبَثُونَ" before continuing the verse.]» ﴿مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ لِيُخْرِجوكَ مِنْهَا وَإِذاً لاَّ يَلْبَثُونَ خِلافَكَ إلاَّ قَليلاً﴾ (from the land, to expel you from it; and then they would not have remained after you except a little). He says: had you gone out while they did not believe, the punishment would have come down upon them.

farraa:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿سُنَّةَ مَن قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ﴾ ([this is] the way of those We sent before you): "the way" (السنّة) is accusative on the basis of the suppressed (verb of) punishment, i.e. they will be punished according to the way of those We had sent; ﴿وَلاَ تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنَا تَحْوِيلاً﴾ (and you will not find in Our way any alteration).

farraa:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلاَةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ (establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night): it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: it is its declining and its passing the meridian, for the noon prayer. Abū Zakariyyā said: I have seen the Arabs take الدلوك to mean the setting of the sun. One of them recited to me:
هذا مَقَام قدَمَىْ رَبَاحِ * ذبَّبَ حتى دَلكَتْ بِرَاحِ
(This is where the two feet of Rabāḥ stood: he kept (people) off until the sun set — "bi-rāḥ".)
He means the water-drawer; ذبَّب: he drove the people away. بِرَاح: he says: until he put his palm (al-rāḥa) over his eye to see whether it had set. He said: that is how they explained it.
His saying ﴿إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾: the beginning of its darkness, for the sunset and evening prayers.
His saying ﴿وَقُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ﴾ (and the recitation at dawn): i.e. and establish the dawn recitation. ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُوداً﴾ (indeed the dawn recitation is ever witnessed) means the dawn prayer, which the angels of the night and the angels of the day attend.

farraa:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿نَافِلَةً لَّكَ﴾ (as an additional [prayer] for you): there is no nāfila (supererogatory act) for anyone except the Prophet ﷺ, because there is no one who does not fear for himself, whereas the Prophet ﷺ has been forgiven his past and future sins, so his (extra) deeds are a nāfila.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿وَقُل رَّبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ﴾ (and say: "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance"): He said it to him on the way back, when he returned from his camp to Medina, at the time he intended (to go to) Syria. ﴿وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ﴾ (and cause me to exit a sound exit): to Mecca.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿كَانَ يَئُوساً﴾ (he is despairing): if you drop the hamza of His saying ﴿يؤوساً﴾, the Arabs say يَوْساً and يَوْوْساً, combining two vowelless letters. Likewise ﴿وَلاَ يَؤودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا﴾ (and their preservation does not tire Him), and likewise ﴿بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ﴾ (with a wretched punishment): one says بَيْسِ and (بَيْيْسٍ), and (ويؤوده), combining two vowelless letters. This is the speech of the Arabs. The readers, however, say (يَوُوساً) and (يَوُوده), moving the wāw toward ḍamma, and (بَيِيْسٍ), moving the first yāʾ toward kasra. We have not found that in their speech, because vowelling the yāʾ and the wāw is heavier than dropping the hamza, and they would not go from something heavy to something heavier still.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِ﴾ (say: each works according to his manner): (شاكلته is) his direction, and it is the way and the disposition (الجديلة). I heard some Arabs of Quḍāʿa say: "ʿAbd al-Malik at that time was on his course (جديلته), and Ibn al-Zubayr on his course." The Arabs say: "so-and-so is on a good way (طريقة)", "a good خَيْدَبة", and "سُرْجُوجة"; and ʿUkl say: سِرْجِيجة.

farraa:85-85.t: His saying: ﴿قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي﴾ (say: the spirit is of the affair of my Lord): he says: of the knowledge of my Lord, not of your knowledge.

farraa:87-87.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾ (except as a mercy from your Lord) is an istithnāʾ (exception), like His saying ﴿إلاَّ حَاجَةً فىِ نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا﴾ (except a need in Jacob's soul which he satisfied).

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَن يَأْتُواْ بِمِثْلِ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ لاَ يَأْتُونَ﴾ (to produce the like of this Qurʾān, they could not produce): (لا يأتون) is the answer to His saying ﴿لئِن﴾ (if). When the Arabs answer (لئِن) with (لا), they make what comes after لا nominative, because (لئِن) is like an oath, and the answer of an oath with (لا) is nominative. Sometimes a poet uses the jussive, because (لئن) is the conditional إن with a lām added to it, so the verb in it is directed to (the past form) فَعَل; were the يفعل (imperfect) form brought, its being jussive would be permitted. Some poets used the jussive with لئِن, and some with the لا that is its answer. Al-Aʿshā said:
لئن منُيتَ بنا عن غِبّ معركَة * لا تُلْفِنا من دماء القوم نَنتفل
