Or ﴿أن﴾ is explicative, and the clause after it is explicative, with no grammatical position. ﴿لا﴾ is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾; ﴿وكيلًا﴾ is the first object of تتخذوا; and ﴿من دوني﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second object of ﴿تتخذوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ذرية من حملنا مع نوح﴾: ذرية is made accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ); it has been said: as a vocative; it has been said: as a badal (substitute) from ﴿وكيلًا﴾; and it has been said: as the second object of تتخذوا; ﴿مَن﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿حملنا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿مع﴾ is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حملنا﴾, and نوح is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿إنه كان عبدا شكورا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and the hāʾ its noun (ism); كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; عبدًا is its khabar (predicate), and شكورًا a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; قضينا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إلى بني إسرائيل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قضينا﴾; and ﴿في الكتاب﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿لتفسدن في الأرض مرتين﴾: the lām is the answer to the omitted oath, or the decisive decree is treated as an oath, as though it were said: "and We swore: you will surely cause corruption"; تفسدن is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the presence of the nūn, which has been elided because of the succession of nūns; the wāw of the plural, elided because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; ﴿في الأرض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تفسدن﴾; ﴿مرتين﴾ is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is its number, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ because it is dual.
﴿ولتعلن علوا كبيرا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿لتعلن﴾ is conjoined to لتفسدن, and it is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the presence of the nūn, which has been elided because of the succession of nūns; the wāw of the plural, elided because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; ﴿علوًّا﴾ is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq, and كبيرًا a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فإذا جاء وعد أولاهما بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا أولي بأس شديد﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; the clause ﴿جاء﴾ is that to which the adverb is annexed (muḍāf ilayhi); ﴿وعد﴾ is the fāʿil (agent) and أولاهما muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and an omitted muḍāf must be supposed, i.e. "the promise of the punishment of the first of them"; the clause ﴿بعثنا﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; ﴿عليكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بعثنا﴾; عبادًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أولي﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عبادًا﴾; ﴿بأس﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; and ﴿شديد﴾ is a naʿt of بأس. [Translator's note: the source does not parse لنا.]
﴿فجاسوا خلال الديار﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; جاسوا is conjoined to ﴿بعثنا﴾; ﴿خلال﴾ is an adverb of place attached to ﴿جاسوا﴾, and الديار is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وكان وعدا مفعولا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; ﴿كان﴾ is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, and its noun (ism) is a pronoun referring back to the promise of punishment; ﴿وعدًا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and مفعولًا a naʿt of ﴿وعدًا﴾; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Or the wāw is parenthetical, and the clause is a parenthesis between the two conjoined items, with no grammatical position. It has been said: the wāw conjoins to ﴿بعثنا﴾, and it has been said: it conjoins to ﴿فجاسوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ثم رددنا لكم الكرة عليهم﴾: ثم is a conjunction for delay; ﴿رددنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رددنا﴾; ﴿الكرة﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿عليكم﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah has عليهم] is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿الكرة﴾, or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from it.
﴿وأمددناكم بأموال وبنين وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; أمددناكم is conjoined to ﴿رددنا﴾, and it is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بأموال﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أمددناكم﴾; ﴿بنين﴾ is conjoined to أموال; ﴿جعلناكم﴾ is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; ﴿أكثر﴾ is a second object; and نفيرًا is a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها﴾: إن is conditional; أحسنتم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿أحسنتم﴾ is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿إن أسأتم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿إن أحسنتم﴾; the fāʾ links the answer; and ﴿لها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then your evil-doing [is against them]". [Translator's note: the source does not parse لأنفسكم.]
﴿فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسوءوا وجوهكم﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; إذا is a future adverb of time; ﴿جاء وعد﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil, and الآخرة is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿ليسوءوا﴾: the lām is for giving the reason, and يسوءوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted answer of idhā, i.e. "We sent them so that they might disgrace"; and وجوهكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وليدخلوا المسجد كما دخلوه أول مرة﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ليدخلوا is conjoined to ليسوءوا, i.e. it is attached to something omitted, namely "We sent them"; المسجد is accusative by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); ﴿كما﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "an entering like their entering"; ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar that is genitive by annexation; and ﴿أول مرة﴾ is accusative as an adverb.
﴿وليتبروا ما علوا تتبيرا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ليتبروا is conjoined to ليسوءوا, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; ﴿ما﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يتبروا﴾. It has been said: ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya and temporal (ẓarfiyya), the object of ﴿يتبروا﴾ being omitted, and the adverb attached to ﴿يتبروا﴾; and ﴿تتبيرًا﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم وإن عدتم عدنا وجعلنا جهنم للكافرين حصيرا﴾: ﴿عسى﴾ is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope; ﴿ربكم﴾ is its noun (ism); an with what it governs is in the position of the accusative as khabar (predicate); the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; ﴿عدتم﴾ is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿عدتم﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿عدنا﴾ is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause ﴿عدنا﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); جعلنا is conjoined to عدنا, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; جهنم is a first object; ﴿للكافرين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حصيرًا﴾, and ﴿حصيرًا﴾ is a second object; or ﴿للكافرين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿حصيرا﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and هذا its noun (ism); القرآن is a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative; يهدي is a verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) being omitted, i.e. "guides people", and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿للتي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يهدي﴾; ﴿هي﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أقوم a khabar, and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا كبيرا﴾: ﴿ويبشر﴾ is conjoined to يهدي; المؤمنين is a mafʿūl bihi; الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المؤمنين﴾; the clause يعملون is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; الصالحات is a mafʿūl bihi; أن is an abrogating particle; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar of anna, and أجرًا is its postponed noun; anna with what falls within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿يبشر﴾; and كبيرًا is a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما﴾: ﴿وأن الذين﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أن لهم أجرًا كبيرًا﴾, or conjoined to ﴿يبشر﴾ with something implied, i.e. "and He informs that those who do not believe will be punished"; the clause ﴿أعتدنا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of anna; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعتدنا﴾; عذابًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and أليمًا a naʿt (adjective). [Translator's note: the source does not parse لا يؤمنون بالآخرة.]

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿يدع الإنسان﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بالشر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or to ﴿يدع﴾; ﴿دعاءه﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿بالخير﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, likewise attached to an omitted ḥāl, or attached to الدعاء, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
﴿وكان الإنسان عجولا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial; كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, الإنسان its noun (ism), and عجولا its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين فمحونا آية الليل﴾: the wāw is resumptive; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); الليل is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), النهار is conjoined to الليل, and آيتين is a second object; the clause ﴿وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿فمحونا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and محونا is conjoined to جعلنا; and آية الليل is a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وجعلنا آية النهار مبصرة لتبتغوا فضلا من ربكم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; آية النهار is a first object and مبصرة a second object; ﴿لتبتغوا﴾: the lām is for giving the reason, تبتغوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) His words ﴿وجعلنا﴾; فضلًا is a mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿من ربكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تبتغوا﴾, and [or] a naʿt (adjective) of His words ﴿فضلا﴾.
﴿ولتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب وكل شيء فصلناه تفصيلا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لتعلموا is conjoined to ولتبتغوا; عدد السنين is a mafʿūl bihi, and الحساب is conjoined to عدد; ﴿وكل شيء﴾ is accusative by ishtighāl (the verb being occupied with a pronoun referring to it); ﴿فصلناه﴾ is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; and تفصيلًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; كل إنسان is accusative by ishtighāl (the verb being occupied with a pronoun referring to it); ألزمناه is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); طائره is a second object; and ﴿في عنقه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being".
﴿ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; نخرج is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu"; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نخرج﴾; كتابًا is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿يلقاه﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كتابًا﴾; and ﴿منشورًا﴾ is a second naʿt of ﴿كتابًا﴾, or a ḥāl. [Translator's note: the source does not parse يوم القيامة.]

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا﴾: the clause ﴿اقرأ كتابك﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the object of an omitted saying, i.e. "it will be said to him"; اقرأ is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; كتابك is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كفى﴾ is a past verb; ﴿بنفسك﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿نفسك﴾ is the fāʿil, nominative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in form; اليوم is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عليك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿حسيبًا﴾; and حسيبًا is a tamyīz (specification), and it has been said: a ḥāl, because it is a derived word.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه﴾: من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); اهتدى is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿فإنما﴾: the fāʾ is linking, and إنما is inna restrained by the restraining mā (kāffa wa-makfūfa); يهتدي is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; ﴿لنفسه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يهتدي﴾; and the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها﴾: conjoined to the preceding clause; ﴿عليها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted that is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "his straying falling upon it".
﴿ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لا is negating; تزر is an imperfect verb and [وازرة] its fāʿil; وزر is the object of ﴿تزر﴾, and أخرى is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ما is negating; ﴿كنا﴾ is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, ﴿نا﴾ its noun (ism), and معذبين its khabar (predicate); ﴿حتى﴾ is a particle of limit and a preposition; نبعث is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after ﴿حتى﴾; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive by ﴿حتى﴾, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of kāna [Translator's note: so in the source]; and رسولًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وإذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها﴾: the wāw is resumptive; إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; the clause أردنا is that to which the adverb is annexed (muḍāf ilayhi); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and what falls within its scope is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أردنا﴾; قرية is the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿نهلك﴾; the clause أمرنا has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of idhā; مترفيها is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ففسقوا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and فسقوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿فيها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فسقوا﴾.
﴿فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ﴿حق﴾ is a past verb; ﴿عليها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿حق﴾; القول is the fāʿil; ﴿فدمرناها﴾ is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; and تدميرًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿وكم أهلكنا من القرون من بعد نوح﴾: كم is declarative (khabariyya), in the position of the accusative as the object of أهلكنا; ﴿من القرون﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is accusative as the tamyīz (specification) of ﴿كم﴾; ﴿من بعد نوح﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or to ﴿أهلكنا﴾, ﴿مِن﴾ being for the beginning [of time].
﴿وكفى بربك بذنوب عباده خبيرا بصيرا﴾: the bāʾ is connective (ṣila); ﴿ربك﴾ is the fāʿil (agent), nominative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in form; ﴿بذنوب عباده﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خبيرًا بصيرًا﴾; and ﴿خبيرا بصيرا﴾ are two accusative tamyīzes.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد﴾: من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause ﴿يريد العاجلة﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of kāna; ﴿عجلنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and it is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عجلنا﴾; ﴿فيها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿ما﴾ is a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause نشاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿لمن﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) from ﴿له﴾ with repetition of the governing word; the clause ﴿نريد﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position, and the object of نريد is omitted, i.e. "for whom We will to hasten it"; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of ﴿مَن﴾.
﴿ثم جعلنا له جهنم يصلاها مذموما مدحورا﴾: ثم is a conjunction for delay; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted second object of جعلنا; جهنم is the first object of جعلنا; the clause ﴿يصلاها﴾ is a ḥāl from the pronoun in ﴿له﴾; مذمومًا is a ḥāl from the pronoun in ﴿يصلاها﴾, and ﴿مدحورًا﴾ is also a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and the clause is conjoined to the one before it; ﴿سعى لها﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أراد﴾; ﴿سعيها﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and it has been said: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the meaning is "and did for it its deed".
﴿وهو مؤمن﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مؤمن a khabar (predicate); the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ﴿سعى﴾.
﴿فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا﴾: the fāʾ links the answer of man; أولئك is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, سعيهم its noun (ism), and مشكورا its khabar; the clause is the khabar of أولئك; and the clause ﴿أولئك كان...﴾ etc. is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿كلا نمد هؤلاء وهؤلاء من عطاء ربك﴾: كلًّا is a fronted object of ﴿نمد﴾; the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿نمد﴾ is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu"; هؤلاء is a badal (substitute) from ﴿كلًّا﴾, and هؤلاء is conjoined to the first هؤلاء; and ﴿من عطاء ربك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نمد﴾.
﴿وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial; ﴿ما﴾ is negating; كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, عطاء its noun (ism), and محظورا its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض﴾: انظر is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); فضلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; بعضهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿على بعض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فضلنا﴾.
﴿وللآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; the lām is the lām of inception (ibtidāʾ); الآخرة is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أكبر a khabar (predicate); درجات is a tamyīz (specification), accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; أكبر is conjoined to the first أكبر; and تفضيلًا is a tamyīz.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿لا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتقعد مذموما مخذولا﴾: لا is prohibitive; تجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta"; ﴿مع الله﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted second object of تجعل; إلهًا is the first object of تجعل, and آخر a naʿt (adjective); ﴿فتقعد﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation, and تقعد is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the fāʾ of causation; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar understood from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there not be from you a making, and so a sitting". The fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "anta"; مذمومًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and مخذولًا a second ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; قضى ربك is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿ألّا﴾: ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya and ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿تعبدوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿أن﴾, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾ and what it governs is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قضى﴾. The clause ﴿لا تعبدوا﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is explicative, because ﴿قضى﴾ contains the meaning of "said", and the clause after it is explicative, with no grammatical position; ﴿لا﴾ is then prohibitive, and ﴿تعبدوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿إلا﴾ is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and ﴿إياه﴾ is an object; ﴿بالوالدين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "and do good"; and ﴿إحسانًا﴾ is the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.
﴿إما يبلغن عندك الكبر أحدهما أو كلاهما﴾: إن is conditional and ﴿ما﴾ is for emphasis; يبلغن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿عندك﴾ is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); أحدهما is the fāʿil of ﴿يبلغن﴾; ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction; and ﴿كلاهما﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أحدهما﴾, the sign of its nominative being the alif, because it is treated like the dual. [Translator's note: the source does not parse الكبر.]
﴿فلا تقل لهما أف ولا تنهرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما﴾: the fāʾ links the answer; ﴿لا﴾ is prohibitive; ﴿تقل﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive by ﴿لا﴾; ﴿لهما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تقل﴾; ﴿أف﴾ is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) with the sense of an imperfect verb, meaning vexation, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anā", and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿ولا تنهرهما﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لا تقل لهما﴾; ﴿قل﴾ is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "anta"; ﴿لهما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قل﴾; ﴿قولًا﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative with the fatḥa; and ﴿كريمًا﴾ is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة﴾: ﴿واخفض لهما﴾ is conjoined to ﴿وقل لهما﴾; جناح الذل is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿من الرحمة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اخفض﴾, or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وقل رب ارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿قل﴾ is conjoined to what preceded; ﴿رب﴾ is a vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker, the vocative particle having been omitted from it; ﴿ارحمهما﴾ is a verb of supplication; ﴿كما﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "have mercy on them with a mercy like their rearing of me"; ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya; ﴿ربياني﴾ is a past verb, the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar formed from ﴿ما﴾ and the verb is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and صغيرًا is a ḥāl from the yāʾ.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿ربكم أعلم بما في نفوسكم﴾: ربكم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أعلم a khabar (predicate); ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعلم﴾; and ﴿في نفوسكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿إن تكونوا صالحين فإنه كان للأوابين غفورا﴾: the clause is circumstantial; إن is conditional; تكونوا is an incomplete, abrogating imperfect verb, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the wāw is its noun (ism) and صالحين its khabar; the fāʾ links the answer; إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the hāʾ its noun, and the clause ﴿كان﴾ its khabar; للأوابين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿غفورًا﴾; and غفورًا is the khabar of kāna.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ولا تبذر تبذيرا﴾: ﴿آت﴾ is an imperative verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "anta"; ﴿ذا القربى﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and ﴿حقه﴾ a second object; المسكين and ابن السبيل are conjoined to ﴿ذا القربى﴾; ﴿لا﴾ is prohibitive; تبذر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾; and تبذيرًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and المبذرين its noun (ism); كانوا is an incomplete, abrogating past verb and the wāw its noun; إخوان الشياطين is the khabar (predicate) of kāna; and the clause كانوا is the khabar of inna.
﴿وكان الشيطان لربه كفورا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial; كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb and الشيطان its noun; ﴿لربه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كفورًا﴾; كفورًا is the khabar of kāna; and an omitted muḍāf must be supposed, i.e. "to the favours of his Lord and His blessings".

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وإما تعرضن عنهم ابتغاء رحمة من ربك ترجوها﴾: ﴿وإما﴾: إن is conditional and ﴿ما﴾ is connective (ṣila); تعرضن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it is in the position of the jussive; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; ﴿عنهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعرضن﴾; ابتغاء رحمة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or [it belongs to] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), having been placed before it, i.e. "then say to them a gracious, gentle word, and promise them a fair promise to gladden their hearts, seeking mercy from your Lord"; ﴿من ربك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رحمة﴾; and the clause ﴿ترجوها﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from رحمة, or a second naʿt.
﴿فقل لهم قولا ميسورا﴾: the fāʾ is linking; قل is an imperative verb; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قل﴾; ﴿قولًا﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative with the fatḥa. ميسورًا is a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; يدك is the first object of تجعل and مغلولة the second object of تجعل; and ﴿إلى عنقك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مغلولة﴾.
﴿ولا تبسطها كل البسط﴾: ﴿ولا تبسطها﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لا تجعل﴾. ﴿كل﴾ is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿البسط﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فتقعد ملوما محسورا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation; تقعد is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the fāʾ preceded by a prohibition; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar understood from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there not be from you a spreading, and so a sitting". The fāʿil of ﴿تقعد﴾ is latent, its implied form being "anta"; ملومًا and محسورًا are two ḥāls (circumstantials), or two khabars (predicates) of ﴿تقعد﴾ if it is taken to contain the meaning of "become".

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿إن ربك يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), ربك its noun (ism), and the clause ﴿يبسط﴾ its khabar (predicate); الرزق is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يبسط﴾; the clause يشاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position; and يقدر is conjoined to يبسط.
﴿إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle and the hāʾ its noun; كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, and its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; ﴿بعباده﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خبيرًا بصيرًا﴾; ﴿خبيرًا بصيرًا﴾ are two khabars of ﴿كان﴾; and the clause كان is the khabar of inna.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق﴾: لا is prohibitive; تقتلوا is jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾; أولادكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); خشية is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and إملاق muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿نحن نرزقهم وإياكم﴾: نحن is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause نرزقهم a khabar (predicate); إياكم is conjoined to the hāʾ.
﴿إن قتلهم كان خطئا كبيرا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and قتلهم its noun (ism); كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb; خطئًا is the khabar of kāna, and its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; the clause ﴿كان﴾ is the khabar of inna; and كبيرًا is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿خطئًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t: ﴿ولا تقربوا الزنا إنه كان فاحشة وساء سبيلا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تقربوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الزنا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿إنه﴾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position; إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and the hāʾ its noun (ism); كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa", and فاحشة its khabar (predicate); the clause كان is the khabar of inna; ﴿ساء﴾ is a past verb for blame, its fāʿil latent; سبيلًا is a tamyīz (specification); and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "it".

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and لا تقتلوا is conjoined to what preceded; النفس is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and ﴿التي﴾ a naʿt (adjective); the clause حرم الله is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿بالحق﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تقتلوا﴾, the bāʾ being causal; or [attached] to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of تقتلوا, i.e. "accompanied by the right".
﴿ومن قتل مظلوما﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); قتل is a past verb in the passive (built for what has not had its agent named), in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; and مظلومًا is a ḥāl.
﴿فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا﴾: the fāʾ is linking; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿لوليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted second object of جعلنا; and سلطانًا is the first object of جعلنا.
﴿فلا يسرف في القتل﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; يسرف is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and its fāʿil is latent, referring back to the guardian; and ﴿في القتل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يسرف﴾.
﴿إنه كان منصورا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the hāʾ its noun (ism), and the clause كان its khabar (predicate); كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, its noun is latent, and ﴿منصورًا﴾ is the khabar of kāna; the clause ﴿إنه...﴾ gives the reason.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and لا تقربوا is also conjoined; ﴿مال اليتيم﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿بالتي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted excepted item, i.e. "do not approach it in any state at all except with the trait or way that is best"; ﴿هي﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أحسن a khabar (predicate), and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.
﴿حتى يبلغ أشده﴾: حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; ﴿يبلغ﴾ is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied ﴿أن﴾ after ḥattā; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تقربوا. [Translator's note: the source does not parse أشده.]
﴿وأوفوا بالعهد﴾: أوفوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿بالعهد﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أوفوا﴾.
﴿إن العهد كان مسئولا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), العهد its noun (ism), and the clause كان its khabar; كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), and مسئولًا its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun have been omitted for lightness, i.e. "about it".

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; أوفوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الكيل is the object of أوفوا; إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; the clause ﴿كلتم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and its answer is omitted, indicated by His words أوفوا الكيل; and ﴿زنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أوفوا الكيل﴾.
﴿ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا﴾: ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿خير﴾ a khabar (predicate); أحسن is conjoined to خير; and ﴿تأويلًا﴾ is a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم﴾: لا is prohibitive; ﴿تقف﴾ is jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, namely the wāw, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; ﴿ما﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿ليس﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and it has been said: attached to what ﴿لك﴾ is attached to, namely "being established (al-istiqrār)"; and ﴿علم﴾ is the postponed noun (ism) of laysa.
﴿إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and السمع its noun; البصر and الفؤاد are conjoined to السمع; ﴿كل﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أولئك muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, and its noun is latent; ﴿عنه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مسئولًا﴾; مسئولًا is the khabar of kāna; the clause ﴿كان﴾ is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ﴿كل﴾; and the clause ﴿كل أولئك﴾ is the khabar of inna.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا﴾: لا is prohibitive; تمش is jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; ﴿في الأرض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تمش﴾; and مرحًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "your being exultant", and it has been said: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
﴿إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the kāf its noun (ism), and the clause ﴿لن تخرق الأرض﴾ its khabar (predicate); ﴿لن تبلغ الجبال﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لن تخرق﴾; طولًا is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the fāʿil, i.e. "and your height will not reach the mountains"; it has been said: ﴿طولا﴾ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, or an object of purpose; and the clause ﴿إنك﴾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿كل ذلك كان سيئه عند ربك مكروها﴾: كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ذلك muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, and ﴿سيئه﴾ its noun (ism); ﴿عند ربك﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مكروهًا﴾; and مكروهًا is the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿ذلك مما أوحى إليك ربك من الحكمة﴾: ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿مما﴾ a khabar (predicate); the clause أوحى is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿إليك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أوحى﴾; ربك is the fāʿil (agent); and ﴿من الحكمة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted returning pronoun of the relative, i.e. "of what He revealed to you, it being of wisdom", or a ḥāl from the relative ﴿ما﴾.
﴿ولا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and لا تجعل is conjoined to what preceded; ﴿مع﴾ is an adverb of place attached to an omitted second object of ﴿تجعل﴾; ﴿إلهًا﴾ is a first object, and آخر a naʿt (adjective).
﴿فتلقى في جهنم ملوما مدحورا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; ﴿في جهنم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تلقى﴾; and ملومًا and مدحورًا are two ḥāls. [Translator's note: the source does not state the case of تلقى itself.]

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿أفأصفاكم ربكم بالبنين﴾: the hamza is for interrogation of disapproval; ﴿أصفاكم﴾ is a past verb and the kāf its object, and it is conjoined to something omitted, supposed according to the context; ﴿ربكم﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); and ﴿بالبنين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أصفاكم﴾.
﴿واتخذ من الملائكة إناثا﴾: ﴿اتخذ﴾ is a verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, and it is conjoined to أصفاكم; ﴿من الملائكة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted second object of اتخذ; and إناثًا is a first object. It has been said: the wāw is the wāw of circumstance, the clause ﴿اتخذ من الملائكة إناثًا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and qad is implied.
﴿إنكم لتقولون قولا عظيما﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and the kāf its noun (ism); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause تقولون is its khabar (predicate); ﴿قولًا﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative with the fatḥa. عظيمًا is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن ليذكروا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; the lām occurs in the answer of an implied (muqaddar) oath; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); صرفنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and its object is omitted, i.e. "parables, admonitions and rulings"; ﴿في هذا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿صرفنا﴾, and القرآن is a badal (substitute); the lām is for giving the reason, and يذكروا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to صرفنا.
﴿وما يزيدهم إلا نفورا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; ما is negating; يزيدهم is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and نفورًا is the second object of ﴿يزيدهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿قل لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون﴾: قل is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; لو is conditional; ﴿معه﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna, and آلهة is its postponed noun (ism); ﴿كما يقولون﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a being like their saying"; and ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar that is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا﴾: إذًا is a particle of answer and requital, inoperative; the lām occurs in the answer of law; the clause ﴿ابتغوا﴾ is an answer to the saying of the polytheists, with no grammatical position; the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿إلى ذي العرش﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ابتغوا﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿سبيلًا﴾; and سبيلًا is the object of ابتغوا.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا﴾: سبحانه: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿تعالى﴾ is a past verb conjoined to what the maṣdar (verbal noun) implies, the implied meaning being "He is transcendent and exalted"; ﴿عما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) it; the clause يقولون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; علوًّا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, because it is a maṣdar standing in the place of taʿālī (exaltation); and كبيرًا is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن﴾: تسبح is an imperfect verb; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تسبح﴾; السماوات is the fāʿil (agent) and السبع a naʿt (adjective); الأرض is conjoined to السماوات; ﴿مَن﴾ is conjoined to السماوات and الأرض; and ﴿فيهن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; إن is negating; من is a connective (ṣila) preposition; شيء is genitive (majrūr) in form and nominative (marfūʿ) in position; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); يسبح is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa", and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of شيء; ﴿بحمده﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by His praise".
﴿ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; لكن is an inoperative particle of rectification (istidrāk); لا is negating; تفقهون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and تسبيحهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إنه كان حليما غفورا﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the hāʾ its noun (ism), and the clause كان its khabar; كان is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, and its noun is latent; حليمًا is the first khabar of ﴿كان﴾, and غفورًا its second khabar.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
It is related from Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the meaning of
سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ, and he said: "Declaring Allah free of every evil." Abū Jaʿfar said: the explanation of this is that it means putting Allah, Mighty and Majestic, far away from everything the idolaters ascribed to Him of rivals, opposites, partners and children. According to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. سبّحت الله تسبيحا ("I declared Allah's transcendence with a declaring"); except that when it stands alone it is definite and accusative without tanwīn (nunation), because at its end there are two added letters and it is definite. Sībawayh reported that some of the Arabs make it indefinite and so make it fully declinable. Abū ʿUbayd reported two other ways of explaining its accusative besides this: that it is accusative as a vocative, i.e. يا سبحان الله; and the other way: that it is not qualified. الَّذِي is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). And he said: سرى and أسرى are two well-known dialectal usages. بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا: ليلا is an adverb (ẓarf). مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ: الحرام is a naʿt (adjective) of المسجد. The root sense of حرام is prevention; so the Sacred Mosque is one in which hunting is prohibited. Abū Isḥāq said: the whole sacred precinct (al-ḥaram) is also called a mosque. إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى: الأقصى is a naʿt of it, and likewise الَّذِي بارَكْنا حَوْلَهُ. It is said: the meaning of "We blessed its surroundings" is that the prophets, peace be upon them, who came after Moses ﷺ from the Children of Israel were in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and its surroundings, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, blessed those places by keeping idolatry far from them; and for this reason it was named Bayt al-Maqdis, because it was sanctified (quddisa), i.e. purified, from idolatry. لِنُرِيَهُ is accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay), which stands in place of أن; its origin is the lām of the genitive.

nahhas-irab:2-3.t: وَآتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ: two objects; and likewise وَجَعَلْناهُ هُدىً لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ. أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا with yāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. ألّا يتّخذوا; the source prints the tāʾ form here.]» is the reading of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, the implied form being لئلا يتخذوا ("so that they should not take"). The reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Kufa is أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا; Abū ʿUbayd claimed that it is on the basis of an omission, i.e. "We said to them: do not take". Abū Jaʿfar said: this needs no omission; «أنّ» «[Translator's note: so printed, with shadda; the discussion concerns أن.]» can have the meaning of أي ("that is"), and «أن» can be in the position of the accusative, the meaning being بأن لا تتخذوا ("that you should not take"). The speech was put in the second person because after it comes ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنا in the second person. ذرية is accusative in four ways: it can be a vocative in construct; it can be a badal (substitute) for وكيل, since وكيل has a plural meaning; it and وكيل can be two objects, as you say: لا تتخذ زيدا صاحبا ("do not take Zayd as a companion"); and the fourth way is with the meaning أعني ("I mean"). The nominative is permissible on the reading of whoever read with yāʾ, as a badal for the wāw; but the badal for the wāw is not permissible on the reading of whoever read with tāʾ: one does not say كلّمتك زيدا nor كلمتني زيدا, because the addressee and the addresser need no clarification.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَقَضَيْنا إِلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ: we have mentioned the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that its meaning is "We informed them".
The root sense of قضى in the language is doing a thing in a firm, decisive way; the judge (qāḍī) is the one who makes decisive matters that take effect, and al-qaḍāʾ is the decisive matter that takes effect and cannot be repelled. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū al-ʿĀliya read وَقَضَيْنا إِلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ فِي الْكِتابِ «[Translator's note: the variant reading is not visible in the printed text, which matches the ordinary reading.]», and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir ibn Zayd and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim that they read لَتُفْسِدُنَّ as a verb whose agent is not named (passive). «[Translator's note: i.e. لَتُفْسَدُنَّ; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]» وَلَتَعْلُنَّ, i.e. you will surely become great; the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters and because what precedes it indicates it.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
فَإِذا جاءَ وَعْدُ أُولاهُما بَعَثْنا عَلَيْكُمْ عِباداً لَنا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ: it is said: i.e. We left the way open between you and them. Al-Ḥasan read فجاسوا خلل الديار. Abū Isḥāq said: the root sense of الجوس is seeking a thing exhaustively, i.e. they searched to see whether they could find anyone they had not killed. خِلالَ is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. in the midst of the dwellings.
وَكانَ وَعْداً مَفْعُولًا: وعدا is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and its noun is latent (muḍmar) in it.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ, i.e. We gave you victory over them so that you returned to attack. وَجَعَلْناكُمْ أَكْثَرَ: two objects. نَفِيراً is by way of specification (bayān).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ, i.e. the reward is yours; it is a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَها, i.e. the punishment accrues to it. That لها means عليها is not said by the skilled grammarians; it is an inversion of meaning, and their citing as proof the ḥadīth «اشترطي الولاء لهم» ("stipulate the clientship for them") is worth nothing. There is disagreement over this ḥadīth: a group related it with this wording from the ḥadīth of Mālik ibn Anas, and it is al-Shāfiʿī's narration from him: «واشترطي الولاء لهم». This is a sound, clear meaning. One says اشترط الشيء when one makes it clear, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 266-
فأشرط فيها نفسه وهو معصم
(Gloss: "So he marked himself out in it [i.e. committed himself to the descent], while clinging fast.")
On the other narration «[Translator's note: the source prints the same wording again here; the other narration is presumably «واشرطي».]» the meaning of «واشترطي الولاء لهم» is "for their sake", as you say: "I honour So-and-so for you". There is another view on it: that it has the sense of a prohibition by way of threat and warning.
فَإِذا جاءَ وَعْدُ الْآخِرَةِ, i.e. the promise of the latter time; the adjective was put in the place of the noun it qualifies. The people of Medina and the people of Basra read لِيَسُوؤُا in the plural; the people of Kufa read ليسوء وجوهكم in the singular, except al-Kisāʾī, who read لنسوء وجوهكم and claimed it was the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. From Ubayy ibn Kaʿb there are two narrations: one is that he read (لنسوءن وجوهكم), the lām with fatḥa — it is the lām of the oath with the light nūn, and the pause on it is with alif to distinguish the light from the heavy nūn; and it is related from him (ليسيء وجوهكم) with two yāʾs and a hamza. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The first reading, in the plural, is indicated by وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ كَما دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا ما عَلَوْا. On the second reading there are three views: the meaning is "that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may disgrace"; al-Farrāʾ said: "that the punishment may disgrace"; Abū Isḥāq said: "that the promise may disgrace". The lām in both is the lām of purpose (lām kay), and so too in the third reading. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning being: "and when the promise of the latter time came, We sent them", so this verb is the reply of (إذا), and the lām kay is attached to it. On the meaning of "We sent them" there are two views: one is "We left the way open between you and them and did not make them fear you", so this is figurative: leaving the way open and not instilling fear was made a "sending"; similar to it is أَنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا الشَّياطِينَ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ [Maryam: 83]. The other view: "We sent them against you" means "We commanded them to make war on you when you disobeyed and caused corruption", and this is literal, not figurative. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that for whoever read ليسوآ وجوهكم it is, in his view, the reply without omission, but he implied a verb in «وليتبّروا». Qatāda said: the meaning is "and to destroy that over which they had risen"; someone else said: "and to destroy as long as they remain uppermost". Its true sense in Arabic is "to destroy during the time of their ascendancy", as you say: فلان يؤذيك ما ولي ("So-and-so harms you as long as he holds office").

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: عَسى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the mercy here is the sending of Muḥammad ﷺ. وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ عُدْنا: it is said: if you return to disobedience, We return to withholding victory. وَجَعَلْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ حَصِيراً: two objects.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: إِنَّ هذَا الْقُرْآنَ: القرآن is a naʿt (adjective) of هذا, and the khabar (predicate) is in يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ. وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ: أنّ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. بأنّ ("with the news that").

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسانُ: the wāw was dropped in continuous recitation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. One should not pause on it, because in the written text (al-sawād) it is without wāw; and if someone paused on it outside the Qurʾan, he could only pause with the wāw, because it is the final radical (lām al-fiʿl), which is dropped only in the jussive or in continuous speech; and there is no alif after it. Likewise يدعو and يرجو: the alif comes only with the wāw of the plural, to distinguish it from the wāw that is the final radical in the singular. Al-Akhfash said: it comes in the plural to distinguish it from the wāw of conjunction. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: it comes to distinguish between the accusative pronoun and the emphasising one.
دُعاءَهُ بِالْخَيْرِ: al-Akhfash said: this is as you say انطلقت انطلاقا, i.e. it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "like his praying". Abū Jaʿfar said: the omission of the kāf is not something that requires an accusative or anything else; there is no disagreement among the grammarians that one says عمرو كالأسد ("ʿAmr is like the lion"), and if you omit the kāf you say عمرو الأسد. The true account of the verse is that the implied form is: man prays for evil with a praying like his praying for good; then the adjective was put in the place of the noun it qualifies, and the muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the construct) in the place of the muḍāf.

nahhas-irab:12-13.t: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ آيَتَيْنِ: two objects. Each of them comes in the wake of the other and departs when the other arrives, so they are two signs pointing to One who governs them. فَمَحَوْنا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ, i.e. We did not give it brightness and light like the light of the day; the thing erased is that which is not clearly seen. وَجَعَلْنا آيَةَ النَّهارِ مُبْصِرَةً: it is the sun and its light. لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ: there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "and that you may rest in the night". وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْناهُ تَفْصِيلًا, i.e. We put a separation between one sign and another so that you may take guidance from the proofs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (كل شيء) is accusative by an implied verb, and likewise وَكُلَّ إِنسانٍ أَلْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ. وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ كِتاباً يَلْقاهُ مَنْشُوراً: يلقاه is part of the naʿt (adjective) of كتاب, or if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial). We have mentioned the verse and the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
اقْرَأْ كِتابَكَ: the sign of the jussive and of indeclinability (bināʾ) is the dropping of the ḍamma from the hamza. It is reported from the Arabs: أقر يا هذا ("read, you!"), with the hamza changed; and from this is the saying of Zuhayr: [al-Ṭawīl] 267-
وإلّا يبد بالظّلم يظلم
(Gloss: "…and whoever does not begin with wrongdoing is wronged" — with يبد for يبدأ.)
كَفى بِنَفْسِكَ is in the position of the nominative, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. حَسِيباً is by way of specification (bayān), or if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq said: outside the Qurʾan حسيبة is permissible.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
مَنِ اهْتَدى is a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَإِنَّما يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ; and likewise وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّما يَضِلُّ عَلَيْها, i.e. his deeds are his own. This is indicated by وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى, on whose meaning there are two views: one is that no one is held to account for another's sin; the other is that the meaning is: no one should follow another and imitate him in evil, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ [al-Zukhruf: 22]. One says وزر يزر, the original being يوزر; the wāw was dropped, according to the Basrans, because it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is وزر, وزر and وزرة.
وَما كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا: there are two views on it. One is that the meaning is: We do not punish with the punishment that is a penalty for contravening something that can only be known through being informed, until We send a messenger. The other is that it is the punishment of extermination.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: We have already mentioned وَإِذا أَرَدْنا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها and the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: وَكَمْ is in the position of the accusative, governed by أهلكنا.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْعاجِلَةَ, i.e. who does not want reward in the Hereafter, We do not withhold that from him — لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: كُلًّا is accusative by نمدّ. هؤُلاءِ is a badal (substitute) for كلّ. وَهَؤُلاءِ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it, i.e. We provide for the believer and the unbeliever. وَما كانَ عَطاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُوراً: Saʿīd said, from Qatāda: i.e. diminished.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: كَيْفَ is in the position of the accusative, governed by فضّلنا, except that it is indeclinable (mabnī), not inflected. وَلَلْآخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). دَرَجاتٍ is in the position of the accusative by way of specification (bayān), and likewise تَفْضِيلًا. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: whoever of the people of Paradise is high sees his superiority over whoever is below him, and whoever is beneath him does not see that anyone above him is better than he.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: فَتَقْعُدَ is accusative as the reply to the prohibition.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ is the reading of the people of Medina, the people of Basra and ʿĀṣim; the reading of the people of Kufa except ʿĀṣim is (إمّا يبلغانّ عندك الكبر). The first reading is clearer in Arabic, because أحدهما is singular. The second is permissible, as you say جاءاني أحدهما أو كلاهما ("they came to me, one of them or both of them") as a badal (substitute), because after the verb you have brought in three; the proper form is جاءني أحدهما أو كلاهما. If you wish you may say جاءاني كلاهما أو أحدهما, with كلاهما as tawkīd (emphasis) and أحدهما conjoined.
فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ: there are seven dialectal forms of it. Al-Ḥasan and the people of Medina read (ولا تقل لهما أفّ) «[Translator's note: so printed, with ولا for فلا.]» with kasra and tanwīn (nunation); Abū ʿAmr and the people of Kufa said it with kasra and without tanwīn; the people of Mecca and the people of Syria read it with fatḥa and without tanwīn. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash reported three dialectal forms besides these:
they reported the accusative with tanwīn, the ḍamma with tanwīn, and the ḍamma without tanwīn. Al-Akhfash reported the seventh form; he said: one says أفّي, with the yāʾ retained, as if he said "this saying is for you". Abū Jaʿfar said: in the first reading the kasra is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the tanwīn because it is indefinite, to distinguish it from the definite; it is a good reading, and the basic rule when two quiescent letters meet is kasra. Al-Aṣmaʿī claimed that in such words only tanwīn is permissible, and that Dhū al-Rumma made an error in his saying: [al-Ṭawīl] 268-
وقفنا فقلنا إيه عن أمّ سالم ... وما بال تكليم الدّيار البلاقع
(Gloss: "We halted and said: 'Tell on (īh) about Umm Sālim!' — yet what use is speaking to empty, desolate dwellings?")
Al-Aṣmaʿī was fond of rejecting rare dialectal forms that are not frequent in the speech of the eloquent. As for the skilled grammarians, they say: the tanwīn is dropped on the basis that it is definite, and on this basis are the second reading and the third reading — because the fatḥa is light and the doubling heavy — and the tanwīn is as explained above. The ḍamma without tanwīn is by assimilation (itbāʿ), as one says ردّ; and the tanwīn is as we mentioned, except that al-Akhfash said: tanwīn is ugly when you put it in the nominative, because there is no lām with it in the speech — as if he takes its nominative to be as a mubtadaʾ (subject), as one says ويل له ("woe to him"); and he claimed that the accusative with tanwīn is as one says تعسا له ("may he perish").
وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيماً, i.e. a speech with which you honour them and show them reverence.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ, i.e. from the relative, the orphans, the poor and the wayfarer. ابْتِغاءَ رَحْمَةٍ: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. seeking provision that you are waiting for. فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُوراً: it is said: with gentleness, softness and a promise.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلى عُنُقِكَ: اليد (the hand) is feminine, and العنق (the neck) is treated as masculine and as feminine, masculine being more common, as the poet said: [al-Rajaz] 269-
في سرطم هاد وعنق عرطل
(Gloss: "…with a long gullet, a forward-reaching [head], and a long neck.")
The ḍamma in عنق was dropped because of its heaviness.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ, i.e. He restricts, and does of that whatever contains what is right. This is indicated by إِنَّهُ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ خَبِيراً, i.e. He knows what is good for them. On the meaning of «فتقعد ملوما محسورا» there are two views. One is that of al-Farrāʾ: it is in the status of المحسور, i.e. the worn-out, exhausted one; he reported: حسرت الدّابة فهي محسورة وحسير ("I exhausted the riding animal, so it is exhausted"), when you drive it until it breaks down. The other view is that «محسورا» means one who has been overtaken by regret (ḥasra).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كانَ خِطْأً: خطأ is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, its noun is latent (muḍmar) in it, and the clause is the khabar of inna. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنى: some of the Arabs lengthen it, making it a maṣdar (verbal noun) of زانى, because it only happens between two. إِنَّهُ كانَ فاحِشَةً وَساءَ سَبِيلًا: سبيلا is by way of specification (bayān), i.e. its path is evil and its act foul.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
وَلا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ: we have mentioned it. وَمَنْ قُتِلَ مَظْلُوماً فَقَدْ: مظلوما is a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَقَدْ جَعَلْنا: assimilation (idghām) is good, because the dāl is from the tip of the tongue and the jīm from its middle, so they are close to each other; pronouncing it distinctly is permissible. لِوَلِيِّهِ, i.e. the person nearest to him. سُلْطاناً: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: every سلطان in the Qurʾan is a proof. Abū Isḥāq said: whoever read فَلا يُسْرِفْ فِي الْقَتْلِ made it a statement, i.e. the killer of his kinsman is not to go to excess. «[Translator's note: the statement form would be فلا يسرفُ; the source prints the jussive vowelling.]» إِنَّهُ كانَ مَنْصُوراً: there are five views on the pronoun:
it may refer to the next of kin (al-walī), and this is the most fitting in the view of the people of reasoning, because it is the nearest to it. Ibn Kathīr said, from Mujāhid: the slain man was helped; and this is a good view, because the slain man was helped in this world when the killing of his killer was commanded, and in the Hereafter by an abundant reward and the punishment of his killer. It is said: the killing was helped. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning may be "the killing", because it is an act. «[Translator's note: the source names four positions explicitly before the fifth.]» The fifth view is that of Abū ʿUbayd; he said: it may be that the first killer was helped when he killed. This is the most far-fetched and most strained of them.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كانَ مَسْؤُلًا: everything Allah has commanded is included in this, because He has made a covenant with us concerning it.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
وَلا تَقْفُ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ: included in this is the prohibition of slandering chaste women, of saying about people what one does not know, and of speaking about law and religion on the basis of conjecture, and that no one should say what is not his right. إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤادَ كُلُّ أُولئِكَ كانَ عَنْهُ مَسْؤُلًا: included in this is the prohibition of listening to what it is not lawful to listen to, and of intending and resolving upon what it is not lawful to look at; know that a person is questioned about all of that. He said أولئك of things other than people, because for everything pointed to that is at a distance you may say أولئك, as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 270-
ذمّ المنازل غير منزلة اللّوى ... والعيش بعد أولئك الأيّام
(Gloss: "Blame all dwellings except the dwelling of al-Liwā, and life after those days.")

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
وَلا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحاً, i.e. possessing exultation. Yaʿqūb the reader reported مَرَحاً with kasra on the rāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. مَرِحاً; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]» as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Akhfash said: the kasra on the rāʾ is better, because it is the active participle. Abū Isḥāq said:
the fatḥa on the rāʾ is better, because it contains the sense of emphasis, as one says جاء فلان ركضا ("So-and-so came running"); he made it a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. المرح in the language is insolence and arrogant exultation, and from it come strutting and haughtiness. إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الْأَرْضَ, i.e. your strength will never reach this. وَلَنْ تَبْلُغَ الْجِبالَ طُولًا: so one should not be haughty and exalt oneself.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: «[Translator's note: the entry begins mid-discussion, apparently concerning those who read سَيِّئُهُ (rather than سَيِّئَةً) in كُلُّ ذلِكَ كانَ سَيِّئُهُ.]» They argued from good things that came before, among them وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً and among them وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيماً; and Abū Ḥātim argued from His saying «مكروها», not مكروهة. Abū Jaʿfar said: nothing follows from these arguments, because the good things came earlier in the section of commands; then came the prohibition, and after it came كُلُّ ذلِكَ كانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً, referring to what was forbidden. And He said مكروها and not مكروهة because it refers back to the wording of كلّ, and it is a second khabar (predicate) of the latent pronoun in كان, and that pronoun is masculine.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: إِنَّكُمْ لَتَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) containing the sense of emphasis. عَظِيماً is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: Abū Isḥāq said: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا, i.e. We have indeed made clear. He said: and the meaning of وَما يَزِيدُهُمْ is: the making clear does not increase them إِلَّا نُفُوراً.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
«[Translator's note: the entry refers to عُلُوًّا كَبِيراً, a maṣdar of a different form from its verb تعالى.]» I.e. تعاليا, as the poet said: [al-Wāfir] 271-
وليس بأن تتبّعه اتّباعا
(Gloss: "…and it is not by your following him with a following" — with the maṣdar اتّباع of a different form from the verb تتبّع.)

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّماواتُ السَّبْعُ: with the feminine on the basis of the group, and يسبح with the masculine on the basis of the whole. وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ: the scholars have discussed its meaning. Some of them said: it is the glorification that is known; some said: it is particular (restricted); and some said: its glorification is its pointing to Allah's transcendence, Mighty and Majestic, and they interpreted وَلكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ as an address to the unbelievers who do not draw the inference. It is said:
"but you do not understand" is an address to people in general, and since among them are some who do not understand that, [it is said that] they did not understand. إِنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيماً, i.e. forbearing towards those who do not draw the inference. غَفُوراً to whoever of them repents.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
It is said: these were people who, when they heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting in Mecca to call people, would revile him; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed him that He would put a barrier between them and him so that they would not understand his recitation. Al-Akhfash said:
«مستورا» means ساترا ("concealing"); the passive pattern مفعول may have the meaning of the active فاعل, as one says مشؤوم and ميمون, i.e. شائم and يامن «[Translator's note: printed «ويا من», evidently for «ويامن».]», because the veil is what conceals. Someone else said: the veil is literally "concealed", because it is something hidden from them.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: وَلَّوْا عَلى أَدْبارِهِمْ نُفُوراً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the basis that it is the plural of نافر; and it may be singular on the basis that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَإِذْ هُمْ نَجْوى: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the implied form is: ذو نجوى ("people of secret counsel").

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثالَ, i.e. they said at one time "he is deluded" and at another "he is a sorcerer", to attach falsehood to you. فَضَلُّوا from the path of truth, فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا to it.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: خَلْقاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). جَدِيداً is its naʿt (adjective). جديد has one meaning for masculine and feminine; جديدة for the feminine is a poor dialectal usage according to Sībawayh.

nahhas-irab:50-51.t: قُلْ كُونُوا حِجارَةً أَوْ حَدِيداً أَوْ خَلْقاً مِمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ, i.e. imagine whatever you wish; you must die and be resurrected. These verses were among the greatest proofs of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَنْ يُعِيدُنا — so He, Mighty and Majestic, foretold that they would say this, and foretold that they would shake their heads in deeming what He said to them unlikely, and that they would say, along with shaking their heads or after it: مَتى هُوَ. And it was recited to them «[Translator's note: printed «وتلى», for «وتُلي».]», and the matter turned out just so.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِ: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: people will come out of their graves saying "Glory be to You, and with Your praise". وَتَظُنُّونَ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا: it is said: they only thought this after the reality which creation cannot escape.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
وَقُلْ لِعِبادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ, i.e. the statement which is best. Al-Māzinī said: the meaning is:
"Say to My servants: 'Say', and they will say." إنّ الشيطان ينزغ بينهم, i.e. he incites the unbelievers against the believers.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ: there is an omission in the speech, indicated by what follows; the implied form is: "Say: call on those whom you claimed to be your gods besides Allah, and let them remove harm from you and shift you from straitness and hardship to ease." This is indicated by فَلا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ الضُّرِّ عَنْكُمْ وَلا تَحْوِيلًا, i.e. they will not shift you from straitness and hardship to ease and plenty.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ حَصِيرًا﴾ means "a place of confinement (ḥabs)". It is taken from the expression "ḥaṣartu al-rajul" (I confined the man), when you have detained him, so he is "maḥṣūr" (confined); and "hādhā ḥaṣīruhu", i.e. his place of detention. "Al-ḥaṣīr" is also the woven mat; it was only called ḥaṣīr because its strands are pressed together (ḥuṣirat), some with others. And the side of the body is called "al-ḥaṣīr", because some of the ribs are held together (maḥṣūr) with others.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ هَذا القُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هي أقْوَمُ﴾, i.e. to the state which is the most upright of states, and that is the affirmation of the Oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic — that is, bearing witness that there is no god but Allah — belief in His messengers, and acting in obedience to Him. This is the description of the state which is the most upright of states.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَدْعُ الإنْسانُ بِالشَّرِّ دُعاءَهُ بِالخَيْرِ﴾: the meaning is that a person may well, in anger, call down evil upon himself, his child and his family, just as he prays for good for himself; and no human being has been free of this.

It is related «that the Prophet ﷺ handed over a captive to Sawda bint Zamʿa. He began moaning during the night, so she said to him: "What is the matter with you that you are moaning?" He complained of the pain of the fetter and of captivity, so she loosened his bonds. When she fell asleep, he pulled his hand free and fled. When the Prophet ﷺ rose in the morning he called for him, and was told what had happened to him, so he said: "O Allah, cut off her hands." Sawda then raised her hands, expecting the prayer to be answered and that Allah would cut off her hands. So the Prophet ﷺ said: "I have asked Allah to make my prayer and my curse against anyone of my family who does not deserve it a mercy. So tell her: I am a human being; I become angry as human beings become angry. Let Sawda lower her hands."»

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that man was created hasty; this is what the whole of humankind has been created upon, from Adam to the last of his offspring. "Al-insān" (man) here has the meaning of "al-nās" (people).

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا اللَّيْلَ والنَّهارَ آيَتَيْنِ﴾, i.e. two signs, which indicate that their Creator is One, there being nothing like unto Him, and which indicate the number of years and the reckoning. ﴿فَمَحَوْنا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ﴾, i.e. We made the sign of the night indicative of it by its darkness. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا آيَةَ النَّهارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلا مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾, i.e. We made it give you light so that you may see how you go about your work. ﴿وَلِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ والحِسابَ﴾. It is related that the moon used to have the brightness of the sun, and Allah effaced its brightness with the darkness that was placed in it.

﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْناهُ تَفْصِيلا﴾, i.e. We have made it clear with a clarification such that it is not confused with anything else. The preferred reading is the accusative (naṣb) in "كُلَّ". The meaning with the accusative is: "so that you may seek bounty from your Lord, and so that you may know the number of the years, and We have set out everything in detail (wa-faṣṣalnā kulla shayʾin tafṣīlan)". "كُلَّ" is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmar) verb, which the overt one — "فَصَّلْناهُ" — explains. It is also permissible to say "وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْناهُ تَفْصِيلًا" (in the nominative). Likewise the accusative and the nominative are both possible in His saying: ﴿وَكُلَّ إنْسانٍ ألْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ في عُنُقِهِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 13], except that I know of no one who read it in the nominative.

It has come in the exegesis that "طائِرُهُ" (his omen) means "his good and his evil", and it is — and Allah knows best — whatever deed of his of the kind from which one draws an ill omen, as He said: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أوْزارَهم كامِلَةً يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25], and as one says to a person: "my sin is on your neck". Something that clings to a person is spoken of as "this is on the person's neck", i.e. it clings to him as the necklace clings to him, among the things worn on the neck. ﴿وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ كِتابًا يَلْقاهُ مَنشُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 13]: in this there are four possibilities: "وَتُخْرَجُ لَهُ" (and it will be brought out for him); "وَيُخْرِجُ لَهُ", i.e. "and Allah will bring out for him"; "وَيَخْرُجُ لَهُ", i.e. "and his deed will come out for him on the Day of Resurrection as a book"; and likewise "يُخْرَجُ لَهُ عَمَلُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ" (his deed will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection). ﴿كِتابًا يَلْقاهُ مَنشُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 13] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿كَفى بِنَفْسِكَ اليَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا﴾: "بِنَفْسِكَ" is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), even though it is made genitive by the bāʾ. Were it not in the Qurʾān, "كَفى بِنَفْسِكَ اليَوْمَ حَسِيبَةً" (with the feminine) would be permissible. The meaning is: "your self suffices as a reckoner", i.e. "since you bear witness against yourself, this is sufficient for you". "حَسِيبًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى﴾: one says "wazara, yaziru" — so he is "wāzir" — with the verbal nouns "wazran", "wizran" and "zira", and its meaning is "athima, yaʾthamu, ithman" (to sin). There are two interpretations of this verse. One of them is that the sinner and the wrongdoer — no one else is taken to account for his sin. The second interpretation is that a person ought not to commit sin because someone else committed it, as the disbelievers said: ﴿إنّا وجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ وإنّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 22].

His saying: ﴿وَما كُنّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولا﴾, i.e. until We make clear that for which We punish, and that on account of which We admit to Paradise.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا أرَدْنا أنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها﴾: it is read "أمَرْنا", without doubling, on the pattern of "faʿalnā"; it is read "آمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها", on the pattern of "afʿalnā"; and it is read "أمَّرْنا", with the mīm doubled. As for whoever read it without doubling, it is from "al-amr" (command); the meaning is: "We commanded them to obey, but they acted sinfully."

If someone were to say: do you not say "I commanded Zayd and he struck ʿAmr", the meaning being that you commanded him to strike ʿAmr and he struck him, so that this wording indicates nothing other than the striking? [The answer is that] the equivalent of His saying ﴿أمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها﴾ in ordinary speech is "I commanded you, and you disobeyed me": it is known that disobedience is contrary to the command, and likewise sinfulness (fisq) is contrary to the command of Allah, exalted be His praise. [Translator's note: the bracketed words "The answer is that" are added for clarity; the Arabic moves straight from the objection to the reply.]

It has also been said that the meaning of "أمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها" is only "We multiplied its affluent ones", and the evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «"The best of wealth is a row of pollinated palms and a prolific (maʾmūra) filly"», i.e. one made to multiply. The Arabs say "qad amira banū fulān" (the sons of so-and-so have amira) when they have become numerous. The poet said:
؎إنْ يُغْبَطُوا يَهْبِطُوا وإنْ أمِرُوا يَوْمًا يَصِيرُوا لِلْهَلْكِ والنَّفَدِ
(If they are envied [for their prosperity] they decline, and if one day they grow numerous, they come to destruction and depletion.)
It is also narrated as "bi-l-naqd", with qāf.

Whoever read "آمَرْنا", its interpretation is "We made numerous", and the abundance here may be one of two things: one of them is that the number of the affluent increases, and the other is that their wealth and riches increase. Whoever read "أمَّرْنا", with doubling, its meaning is "We gave its affluent ones authority", i.e. We granted them rule and power.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا مِنَ القُرُونِ مِن بَعْدِ نُوحٍ﴾, i.e. We destroyed a great number of generations with various kinds of punishment, such as the people of Lūṭ, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those whose names have been mentioned, ﴿وَقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 38]. The position of "كَمْ" is the accusative, by His saying "أهْلَكْنا".

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿مَن كانَ يُرِيدُ العاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنا لَهُ فِيها ما نَشاءُ لِمَن نُرِيدُ﴾, i.e. whoever by his deeds desires the hasty [world] — that is, this world — Allah hastens to whomever He wishes to hasten it for whatever Allah wills, i.e. not what he himself wills. "Mā yashāʾu" (what He wills) has the meaning of "ما نَشاءُ" (what We will). It is also possible that the implied pronoun in "نَشاءُ" refers to "مَن" (whoever); the meaning would then be: "We hasten for the servant what he desires", if Allah wills that. [Translator's note: the text says the implied pronoun in "نشاء" could refer to "من", although "نشاء" is first-person plural; this is translated as written.]
